summary: Clausen and Mathew define étale K-theory K^et as the étale sheafification of nonconnective K-theory on qcqs E_2-spectral algebraic spaces and show it is accessible. K^et agrees with Selmer K-theory K^Sel = L_1K ×_{L_1TC} TC in degrees ≥ −1 (Theorem 1.1); K → K^et is a p-local isomorphism in degrees ≥ max(d − 2, 0) with d bounded by virtual Galois cohomological dimensions and 1 + log_p[k : k^p] (Theorem 1.2, a Lichtenbaum–Quillen statement in all characteristics); K^et is a Postnikov sheaf under finite dimension hypotheses (Theorem 1.3); and it commutes with filtered colimits (Theorem 1.5). L_n^f-local localizing invariants satisfy étale hyperdescent (Theorem 1.11). Behind these is a study of hypercompleteness of sheaves of spectra. Zariski and Nisnevich topoi of qcqs algebraic spaces of Krull dimension d have homotopy dimension ≤ d without noetherian hypotheses (Theorem 1.7). A sheaf on the site of a profinite group of finite cohomological dimension is hypercomplete iff its Galois actions are uniformly nilpotent (Theorem 1.8), although Tate vanishing does not suffice (Example 4.15, answering Jardine). Étale hypercompleteness is Nisnevich plus Galois hypercompleteness (Theorem 1.6), and étale hypercompletion is smashing (Theorem 1.9). The inputs are Gabber–Suslin rigidity, the rigidity of Clausen–Mathew–Morrow, the norm-residue theorem, Geisser–Levine and Geisser–Hesselholt, and a TC étale-hyperdescent theorem generalizing Geisser–Hesselholt to E_2-bases. The atlas plans derived Postnikov completion (EnhancedDerivedSheaves E2), the norm-residue theorem, motivic filtration and Quillen–Lichtenbaum for fields (MotivicEtaleKTheory M.5–M.7), THH, TC and Dundas–Goodwillie–McCarthy (RefinedTraceMethods), K-theory foundations and Gabber rigidity. The hypercompleteness theory goes to a new Part II of EnhancedDerivedSheaves; E_2-spectral algebraic spaces, chromatic inputs, TC descent, Selmer and étale K-theory to a new Part II of MotivicEtaleKTheory; the Clausen–Mathew–Morrow inputs to the henselian-pairs Part II proposed by that extraction; and standard facts to sources of E2, SF.0 and SF.1. Five misprints are recorded; no error or gap was found.

items.name: Theorem 1.1: étale K-theory agrees with Selmer K-theory in degrees ≥ −1
items.statement: Let X be a qcqs E_2-spectral algebraic space with connective structure sheaf (for instance a qcqs spectral algebraic space, or an ordinary qcqs algebraic space). Then the natural map K^et(X) → K^Sel(X) = L_1K(X) ×_{L_1TC(X)} TC(X) of Construction 7.10 is an isomorphism on π_n for every n ≥ −1. Here K is nonconnective K-theory of Perf(X), K^et its étale sheafification and L_1 Bousfield localization at KU.

items.name: Theorem 1.2: Lichtenbaum–Quillen for étale K-theory
items.statement: Let X be a qcqs E_2-spectral algebraic space of finite Krull dimension and p a prime. For x ∈ X put d_x = vcd_p(k(x)) if char k(x) ≠ p and d_x = 1 + log_p[k(x) : k(x)^p] (= 1 + dim_{k(x)} Ω^1_{k(x)}) if char k(x) = p, and suppose d = sup_x d_x < ∞. Then K(X) → K^et(X) is an isomorphism on p-local homotopy groups in degrees ≥ max(d − 2, 0).
items.note: The introduction states it for qcqs spectral algebraic spaces with d_k = 1 + dim_k Ω^1_{k/k^p} in characteristic p; §7 states it for E_2-spectral algebraic spaces. The proof combines Theorem 7.12(1) with Theorem 6.18(1).

items.name: Theorem 1.3: étale K-theory is a Postnikov sheaf
items.statement: Let X be a qcqs E_2-spectral algebraic space with connective structure sheaf, of finite Krull dimension, with a uniform bound on the virtual 𝒫-local Galois cohomological dimensions of its residue fields (𝒫 a set of primes; 𝒫 = all primes in the introduction). Then K^et_𝒫 is a hypercomplete, equivalently Postnikov complete, sheaf on X_et: it is the limit of its étale-sheafified Postnikov tower, so there is a conditionally convergent descent spectral sequence H^s(X_et; π_t^et K) ⇒ π_{t−s}K^et(X). Moreover every étale sheaf of 𝒫-local spectra on X that is a module over K^et_𝒫 is Postnikov complete.
items.locator: Theorem 1.3, p. 4; Theorem 7.12(2), p. 82; Corollary 4.40, p. 55

items.name: Theorem 1.5: étale K-theory commutes with filtered colimits
items.statement: The functor R ↦ K^et(Spec^et R), from connective E_2-rings (in particular from commutative rings) to spectra, commutes with filtered colimits. Consequently the étale stalks of K^et are the K-theory spectra K^et(A) of strictly henselian local rings A.

items.name: Theorem 1.6: étale hypercompleteness is Nisnevich hypercompleteness plus Galois hypercompleteness
items.statement: Let X be a qcqs algebraic space and F a presheaf of 𝒫-local spectra on et_X. Suppose there is a uniform bound on the 𝒫-local étale cohomological dimension of U_et for all U → X in et_X (or for a cofinal family, e.g. the affine ones). Then F is a hypercomplete étale sheaf if and only if (1) F is a hypercomplete Nisnevich sheaf and (2) for every point x ∈ X the presheaf x^*F on 𝒯_x = 𝒯_{Gal(k(x)^sep/k(x))} (the Nisnevich pullback, Construction 4.33, whose value on a finite étale k(x)-algebra is F of the corresponding finite étale algebra over the henselization) is a hypercomplete sheaf.
items.locator: Theorem 1.6, p. 5; Theorem 4.36, p. 53; proof pp. 53–54
items.note: The paper attributes the result essentially to Thomason ([TT90, Sec. 11]).

items.name: Theorem 1.7 (Zariski): spectral spaces have homotopy dimension at most their Krull dimension
items.statement: Let X be a spectral space of Krull dimension d < ∞ and F a d-connective sheaf of spaces on X. Then F(X) ≠ ∅; that is, Sh(X) has homotopy dimension ≤ d, and if F is (d + n)-connective then F(X) is n-connective. As the hypothesis passes to quasi-compact opens, Sh(X) is locally of homotopy dimension ≤ d, hence Postnikov complete: every sheaf of spaces or spectra on X is hypercomplete, and a map of such sheaves is an equivalence iff it is one on all stalks. Applied to |X| this gives the Zariski half of Theorem 1.7 for a qcqs algebraic space X of finite Krull dimension.
items.locator: Theorem 1.7, p. 6; Theorem 3.12 and the following paragraph, p. 28; proof pp. 29–30
items.note: Cohomological dimension ≤ d was known (Scheiderer [Sch92]); the noetherian case is [HTT, Cor. 7.2.4.17]. Two proofs are given: finite approximation (Lemma 3.13 with Corollary 3.11 and Sancho de Salas) and the Zorn's-lemma argument of Theorem 3.14.

items.name: Theorem 1.7 (Nisnevich): Nisnevich topoi have homotopy dimension at most the Krull dimension
items.statement: Let X be a qcqs algebraic space whose underlying spectral space |X| has Krull dimension ≤ d. Then Sh(X_Nis) has homotopy dimension ≤ d.
items.locator: Theorem 1.7, p. 6; Theorem 3.18, p. 31; proof p. 35
items.note: Known for noetherian schemes: [SAG, Thm. 3.7.7.1], [Nis89], [KS86]. The proof reduces, by Lemma 3.21 and Corollary 3.11, to the p-Nisnevich sites (Corollary 3.25), using that stratifications with dim S ≤ dim |X| are cofinal (Sancho de Salas).

items.name: Theorem 1.8: nilpotence criterion for hypercompleteness on 𝒯_G
items.statement: Let G be a profinite group of finite 𝒫-local cohomological dimension d and F a sheaf of 𝒫-local spectra on 𝒯_G. The following are equivalent: (1) F is hypercomplete; (2) F is Postnikov complete; (3) for every normal inclusion N ⊂ H of open subgroups of G, the spectrum F(G/N) with its H/N-action is d-nilpotent (Definition 4.18: nilpotent of exponent ≤ d + 1 in the sense of [MNN17]); (4) there is d′ ≥ 0 such that F(G/N) is d′-nilpotent as a G/N-spectrum for every open normal N ⊂ G.
items.note: (1) ⇔ (2) is Proposition 2.10; (2) ⇒ (3) is Theorem 4.25 applied to the hypercompletion of the unit; (4) ⇒ (2) is Proposition 4.16 with Lemma 4.19(4). It strengthens the Tate–Thomason vanishing of Tate constructions, whose converse fails (Example 4.15).

items.name: Theorem 1.9: étale hypercompletion is smashing
items.statement: Let X be a qcqs algebraic space of finite Krull dimension with a global bound on the 𝒫-local virtual Galois cohomological dimensions of its residue fields. Then hypercompletion of sheaves of 𝒫-local spectra on X_et is smashing: F^h ≃ F ⊗ S^h, where S^h is the hypercompletion of the constant sheaf on the (𝒫-local) sphere; and it agrees with Postnikov completion. Hence hypersheaves are closed under all colimits and under tensoring with arbitrary sheaves.
items.note: Proved locally by Corollary 4.39 (or by Theorem 4.38(3) and the tensor-ideal property of d-nilpotent objects) and globalized by Proposition 2.25(3).

items.name: Corollary 1.10: modules over étale hypersheaves are hypersheaves
items.statement: Let X be as in Theorem 1.9. Any étale sheaf of spectra on X that is a module over an étale hypersheaf of algebras is itself an étale hypersheaf; in particular every étale sheaf of HZ-modules on X is a hypersheaf.
items.locator: Corollary 1.10, p. 7; Lemma 2.23(5), p. 15; Corollary 4.40, p. 55

items.name: Theorem 1.11: étale hyperdescent for L_n^f-local localizing invariants
items.statement: Let X be a qcqs E_2-spectral algebraic space of finite Krull dimension with a global bound on the mod p virtual cohomological dimensions of its residue fields, and let 𝒜 be a weakly localizing invariant of Perf(X)-linear ∞-categories with values in L_n^f-local spectra (at the prime p). Then Y ↦ 𝒜(Perf(Y)) is an étale hypersheaf on X.
items.note: Strengthens [CMNN], which proved étale descent (not hyperdescent) for E_∞ bases; the proof makes 𝒜 a module over (K_{≥0})^et (Theorem 5.26) and applies Theorems 5.39, 7.12 and Corollary 4.40.

items.name: Grothendieck prestable ∞-categories and sheaves of spectra
items.statement: A Grothendieck prestable ∞-category 𝒞_{≥0} ([SAG, App. C]) has stabilization 𝒞 = Sp(𝒞_{≥0}); the functor 𝒞_{≥0} → 𝒞 is fully faithful onto the connective part of a t-structure whose heart 𝒞^♥ ⊂ 𝒞_{≥0} is a Grothendieck abelian category, with truncations X ↦ X_{≤n} and homotopy objects π_n : 𝒞 → 𝒞^♥ (n ∈ Z). Examples: connective spectra (heart Ab); sheaves of connective spectra on a Grothendieck site 𝒯 (heart the abelian sheaves), where the inclusions, truncations and π_n are computed sectionwise and then sheafified, sheafification being t-exact ([SAG, Rem. 1.3.2.8]); sheaves of connective R-module spectra for a connective E_1-ring R, e.g. R = S_𝒫, the 𝒫-local sphere.

items.name: Acyclic, hypercomplete and Postnikov complete objects
items.statement: An object X of 𝒞 is acyclic if π_nX = 0 for all n; hypercomplete if Hom_𝒞(U, X) ≃ ∗ for every acyclic U; Postnikov complete if X → lim_n X_{≤n} is an equivalence. 𝒞_{≥0} is separated if all objects are hypercomplete, and complete (left-complete) if 𝒞 → lim_n 𝒞_{≤n}, X ↦ {X_{≤n}}, is an equivalence.

items.name: Hypercomplete sheaves of spectra are hypersheaves
items.statement: For a hypercover U_• → X in a site 𝒯 (each U_n a coproduct of objects of 𝒯), colim_{Δ^op} Σ^∞_+h_{U_n} → Σ^∞_+h_X is a π_*-isomorphism of sheaves of spectra ([HTT, Lemma 6.5.3.11]); hence a hypercomplete sheaf of spectra F satisfies F(X) ≃ lim_Δ F(U_n) for all such hypercovers. Conversely hyperdescent implies hypercompleteness ([DHI04], [TV03], [HTT, Cor. 6.5.3.13]). A sheaf of spectra is hypercomplete iff its underlying sheaves of spaces are, and hypercomplete sheaves of spectra are the sheaves of spectra on the hypercompleted ∞-topos ([SAG, Prop. 1.3.3.3]).

items.name: Permanence of hypercompleteness
items.statement: (1) Hypercomplete objects of 𝒞 are closed under all limits. (2) Every t-bounded-above object of 𝒞 is hypercomplete. (3) Postnikov complete objects are hypercomplete; more generally lim_n X_{≤n} is hypercomplete for every X ∈ 𝒞.

items.name: Derived categories of Grothendieck abelian categories are separated but need not be complete
items.statement: For a Grothendieck abelian category 𝒜, 𝒟(𝒜)_{≥0} is a Grothendieck prestable ∞-category ([SAG, Ex. C.1.4.5]); 𝒟(𝒜) has no nonzero acyclic objects, so every object is hypercomplete, but objects of 𝒟(𝒜) need not be Postnikov complete ([Nee11]).

items.name: Cohomological dimension in a prestable ∞-category
items.statement: For U ∈ 𝒞_{≥0} and A ∈ 𝒞^♥, H^i(U; A) = π_0 Map_𝒞(U, Σ^iA). For a collection 𝒜 ⊂ 𝒞^♥, U has cohomological dimension ≤ d with 𝒜-coefficients if H^i(U; A) = 0 for all A ∈ 𝒜 and i > d; 𝒞_{≥0} has enough objects of cohomological dimension ≤ d with 𝒜-coefficients if every X ∈ 𝒞_{≥0} receives a map U → X that is an epimorphism on π_0 from such a U (default 𝒜 = 𝒞^♥). Coproducts of objects of cohomological dimension ≤ d have cohomological dimension ≤ d, so generation under colimits by such objects gives enough of them.

items.name: Finite cohomological dimension: hypercomplete equals Postnikov complete
items.statement: Let X ∈ 𝒞 and suppose 𝒞_{≥0} has enough objects of cohomological dimension ≤ d with {π_nX}_n-coefficients for some d ≥ 0. Then (1) X → lim_n X_{≤n} is a π_*-isomorphism, and (2) X is hypercomplete iff it is Postnikov complete.

items.name: Sites covered by objects of bounded cohomological dimension
items.statement: Let 𝒯 be a Grothendieck site. By [SAG, Cor. 2.1.2.3] the derived ∞-category of abelian sheaves on 𝒯 is the ∞-category of hypercomplete sheaves of HZ-modules, so ∞-topos cohomology is derived-functor cohomology; hence if x ∈ 𝒯 has H^i(x; A) = 0 for all abelian sheaves A and i > d, then h_x has cohomological dimension ≤ d. If every object of 𝒯 is covered by such objects, sheaves of spectra on 𝒯 are hypercomplete iff Postnikov complete; likewise with 𝒫-local cohomological dimension.

items.name: Descent spectral sequence
items.statement: For U ∈ 𝒞_{≥0} and X ∈ 𝒞 there is a conditionally convergent spectral sequence E_2^{s,t} = H^s(U; π_tX) ⇒ π_{t−s} Map_𝒞(U, lim_n X_{≤n}), obtained from the filtered spectrum {Hom_𝒞(U, X_{≤q})}_q, whose colimit vanishes and whose graded pieces are Σ^qπ_qX.

items.name: Hypercompletion is an accessible exact localization
items.statement: The inclusion 𝒞^h ⊂ 𝒞 of the hypercomplete objects has an accessible left adjoint X ↦ X^h (hypercompletion): the acyclic objects form an accessible full subcategory closed under colimits, since direct sums are t-exact in a Grothendieck prestable ∞-category. X → X^h is characterized as the unique π_*-isomorphism to a hypercomplete object; if 𝒞_{≥0} has enough objects of cohomological dimension ≤ d, then X^h = lim_n X_{≤n}.
items.locator: Proposition 2.14, p. 12 (cf. [SAG, Sec. C.3.6]); Remark 2.15, p. 13

items.name: Universal property of hypercompletion
items.statement: For a Grothendieck prestable ∞-category 𝒞_{≥0}, the hypercompletion functor 𝒞_{≥0} → 𝒞^h_{≥0} is the initial exact left adjoint functor to a separated Grothendieck prestable ∞-category.

items.name: Left (Postnikov) completion of a Grothendieck prestable ∞-category
items.statement: The limit of 𝒞_{[0,n]} over n is a complete Grothendieck prestable ∞-category, the universal cocontinuous exact functor out of 𝒞_{≥0} to a complete one; its objects are compatible families X_n ∈ 𝒞_{[0,n]}, and the right adjoint sends {X_n} to lim_n X_n, so the composite is Postnikov completion. Completeness implies every object is Postnikov complete.
items.locator: Construction 2.17 and the following paragraph, p. 13 ([SAG, Prop. C.3.6.3])

items.name: K(1)-acyclic connective spectra: Postnikov completeness without completeness
items.statement: The full subcategory of K(1)-acyclic connective spectra is a Grothendieck prestable ∞-category (K(1)-acyclics are closed under truncations and colimits) in which every object is Postnikov complete, but it is not complete: its left completion is Sp_{≥0}, since the inclusion induces an equivalence on truncated objects.
items.note: Routed with the chromatic inputs (Morava K-theory), which this extraction gives to the Selmer K-theory Part II.

items.name: Countable products criterion for hypercompletion to agree with Postnikov completion
items.statement: Let 𝒞_{≥0} be a Grothendieck prestable ∞-category. If there is d ≥ 0 such that every countable product of truncated objects of 𝒞_{≥0} lies in 𝒞_{≥−d}, then the hypercompletion and the Postnikov completion of 𝒞_{≥0} agree.

items.name: Enough objects of cohomological dimension ≤ d: hypercompletion is Postnikov completion
items.statement: If 𝒞_{≥0} has enough objects of cohomological dimension ≤ d, the hypothesis of Proposition 2.19 holds, so the hypercompletion and the Postnikov completion of 𝒞_{≥0} agree.

items.name: Postnikov completeness of 𝒟(𝒜)_{≥0}
items.statement: Let 𝒜 be a Grothendieck abelian category in which every object is a quotient of an object of cohomological dimension ≤ d. Then 𝒟(𝒜)_{≥0} is Postnikov complete (by Corollary 2.20, as 𝒟(𝒜)_{≥0} is 0-complicial, [SAG, Def. C.5.3.1]).

items.name: Tensor products preserve acyclic objects
items.statement: Let 𝒞_{≥0} carry a symmetric monoidal structure commuting with colimits in each variable (for sheaves of connective spectra on a site, the sheafified smash product, [SAG, Sec. 1.3.4]), extended to 𝒞. (1) If X is acyclic then X ⊗ Y is acyclic. (2) There is a unique symmetric monoidal structure ⊗^h on 𝒞^h making hypercompletion symmetric monoidal, X ⊗^h Y = (X ⊗ Y)^h. (3) Every X ∈ 𝒞^h has a unique functorial 1^h-module structure.

items.name: Characterizations of smashing hypercompletion
items.statement: The following are equivalent: (1) 𝒞^h is closed under colimits and under X ⊗ − for all X ∈ 𝒞; (2) 1^h ⊗ X is hypercomplete for all X; (3) X → 1^h ⊗ X is the hypercompletion of X for all X; (4) Mod_{1^h}(𝒞) → 𝒞 is fully faithful with essential image 𝒞^h; (5) every X ∈ 𝒞 that is a module over an algebra in 𝒞^h lies in 𝒞^h.

items.name: Smashing hypercompletion
items.statement: Hypercompletion is smashing for 𝒞 if the equivalent conditions of Lemma 2.23 hold (compare [Rav84]).

items.name: Local–global principle for hypercompleteness
items.statement: Let 𝔛 be an ∞-topos, x^* : Sh(𝔛, Sp) → Sh(𝔛_{/x}, Sp) the pullback (x^*F)(y → x) = F(y), and S a set of objects covering 𝔛 (the terminal object lies in the colimit closure of S). (1) A sheaf of spectra F is hypercomplete iff x^*F is hypercomplete for all x ∈ S. (2) F is Postnikov complete iff x^*F is for all x ∈ S. (3) If hypercompletion is smashing on each 𝔛_{/x}, x ∈ S, it is smashing on 𝔛. (Whether smashing hypercompletion passes to slices is left open, Remark 2.26.)

items.name: Strongly generating adjunctions
items.statement: A left adjoint F : 𝒞 → 𝒟 between presentable ∞-categories, with right adjoint G, is strongly generating if a diagram f : K^▷ → 𝒟 is a colimit diagram whenever G(f) is. Then G is conservative and the image of F generates 𝒟 under colimits. Example: for a separated Grothendieck prestable 𝒟_{≥0} and X such that every object receives a π_0-surjection from a direct sum of copies of X, tensoring with X from Sp_{≥0} is strongly generating (∞-categorical Gabriel–Popescu, [SAG, Thm. C.2.1.6]).
items.locator: Definition 2.27 and the following paragraph, p. 17

items.name: Criterion for hypercomplete objects to be closed under colimits
items.statement: Let 𝒞_{≥0} be a Grothendieck prestable ∞-category with stabilization 𝒞. Suppose there are d ≥ 0 and a functor h : 𝒯 → 𝒞_{≥0} from a small ∞-category such that (1) the induced PSh(𝒯; Sp) → 𝒞 is strongly generating and (2) for each U ∈ 𝒯 the functors H^n(U; −) = [h_U, Σ^n(−)] : 𝒞^♥ → Ab commute with filtered colimits for all n and vanish for n > d. Then 𝒞^h ⊂ 𝒞 is closed under all colimits, and the hypercompletions of the h_t are compact in 𝒞^h. For sheaves on a site 𝒯, (1) is automatic and hypercomplete sheaves then form a colimit-closed subcategory of PSh(𝒯, Sp).
items.locator: Proposition 2.28 and the following paragraph, pp. 17–18

items.name: Finitary sites and their morphisms
items.statement: A finitary site is a small ∞-category with all finite limits (and, by the paper's convention, a terminal object) and a Grothendieck topology in which every covering sieve is refined by one generated by finitely many elements ([SAG, A.3.1]). A morphism of finitary sites is a finite-limit-preserving functor carrying covering sieves to generators of covering sieves; it induces a geometric morphism Sh(𝒟) → Sh(𝒞) whose pullback sends h_U to h_{F(U)} and whose pushforward is precomposition ([HTT, Prop. 6.2.3.20]).

items.name: Cohomological dimension of a finitary site
items.statement: A finitary site 𝒯 has cohomological dimension ≤ d if Σ^∞_+h_x ∈ Sh(𝒯, Sp_{≥0}) has cohomological dimension ≤ d for every x ∈ 𝒯 (Example 2.11); similarly 𝒫-local cohomological dimension. Then hypercomplete and Postnikov complete agree (Proposition 2.10; cf. [Jar87, Prop. 3.3], [Mit97, Prop. 3.20]), and by Proposition 2.25 the same holds under local finite cohomological dimension.
items.locator: Definition 2.30 and the following paragraph, pp. 18–19

items.name: Sheaves of HZ_𝒫-modules are hypercomplete
items.statement: Let 𝒯 be a finitary site of 𝒫-local cohomological dimension ≤ d which is an ordinary category. Then Sh(𝒯, Mod_{HZ_𝒫}) is hypercomplete.
items.note: Proof via Proposition 2.28, using that cohomology on a finitary site commutes with filtered colimits ([SGA4, Exp. VI.5]).

items.name: Hypercompletion as a limit of truncated tensor products
items.statement: Let 𝒯 be a finitary site of 𝒫-local cohomological dimension ≤ d which is an ordinary category, and F ∈ Sh(𝒯, Sp_{𝒫,≥0}). Then F → lim_n (F ⊗ τ_{≤n}S) exhibits the target as the hypercompletion, equivalently Postnikov completion, of F.

items.name: Nilpotent towers and rapidly converging cosimplicial objects
items.statement: Fix m ≥ 0. A filtered object … → X_{−1} → X_0 → X_1 → … in a stable ∞-category (resp. in Sp) is m-nilpotent (resp. weakly m-nilpotent) if every X_i → X_{i+m+1} is nullhomotopic (resp. zero on π_*); either implies lim X_i ≃ colim X_i ≃ 0. An augmented cosimplicial object X^• ∈ Fun(Δ_+, 𝒞) (resp. in Sp) is m-rapidly converging (resp. weakly m-rapidly converging) if the tower {cofib(X^{−1} → Tot_n X^•)}_n is m-nilpotent (resp. weakly m-nilpotent); it is then a limit diagram.

items.name: Commuting totalizations with filtered colimits
items.statement: Let X_α^•, α ∈ A, be a filtered system of augmented cosimplicial spectra such that each X_α^• is weakly m-rapidly converging for a fixed m. Then colim_α X_α^• is weakly m-rapidly converging, hence a limit diagram, and colim_α Tot(X_α^•) → Tot(colim_α X_α^•) is an equivalence.

items.name: Nilpotence and hyperdescent
items.statement: Let 𝒯 be a finitary site of 𝒫-local cohomological dimension ≤ d and F a sheaf of 𝒫-local spectra on 𝒯. Then F is hypercomplete (equivalently Postnikov complete) iff for every truncated hypercover y_• of an object x ∈ 𝒯 the augmented cosimplicial spectrum F(x) → F(y_•) is d-rapidly converging, equivalently weakly d′-rapidly converging for a constant d′ independent of the hypercover; it suffices to consider truncated hypercovers by finite coproducts of objects of 𝒯.

items.name: Hypercovers lifting π_*-isomorphisms (Dugger–Hollander–Isaksen)
items.statement: Let 𝒯 be a finitary site, F → G a map in PSh(𝒯) inducing an isomorphism on homotopy group sheaves, x ∈ 𝒯 and x → G. Then there is a hypercover y_• of x by finite coproducts of representables with a commutative square |y_•| → F over x → G in PSh(𝒯).
items.note: The inductive construction uses latching and matching objects ([HTT, Prop. A.2.9.14]).

items.name: p-complete étale sheaves on F_p-algebras: hypercomplete equals Postnikov complete
items.statement: Let R be a commutative F_p-algebra. For p-torsion étale sheaves of abelian groups on Spec(R), H^*(Spec(R)_et, F) = 0 for * > 1 ([SGA4, Exp. X, Thm. 5.1] in the noetherian case, and in general by passage to filtered colimits). Hence a sheaf of p-complete spectra on Spec(R)_et is hypercomplete iff it is Postnikov complete.
items.note: Used for the Postnikov claim of Theorem 5.16; the cohomological-dimension input is item 155.

items.name: Homotopy dimension of an ∞-topos
items.statement: In an ∞-topos 𝔛 there are internal notions of n-truncated and n-connective objects ([HTT, Sec. 5.5.6, Def. 6.5.1.10]); for sheaves on a site, F is n-connective (n ≥ 0) iff it is locally nonempty and every class in π_i(F(U), ∗), i < n, is killed on a covering sieve. 𝔛 has homotopy dimension ≤ n if every n-connective object admits a global section ∗ → F; it is locally of homotopy dimension ≤ n if generated under colimits by objects U_α with each 𝔛_{/U_α} of homotopy dimension ≤ n.

items.name: Local finite homotopy dimension implies Postnikov completeness
items.statement: If an ∞-topos 𝔛 is locally of homotopy dimension ≤ n, then the ∞-category Sh(𝔛, Sp) of sheaves of spectra on 𝔛 is Postnikov complete.

items.name: Filtered colimits of finitary sites
items.statement: (1) The ∞-category of finitary sites has filtered colimits, preserved by the forgetful functor to small ∞-categories: on 𝒞 = colim_i 𝒞_i a sieve is covering iff it is refined by the image of a covering sieve of some 𝒞_i. (2) The pushforward Sh(colim_i 𝒞_i) → lim_i Sh(𝒞_i) is an equivalence.
items.locator: Lemma 3.3, pp. 23–24 (classical case [SGA4, Exp. VI, Sec. 7–8])

items.name: Excisive finitary sites
items.statement: A finitary site 𝒞 is excisive if Sh(𝒞) ⊂ PSh(𝒞) is closed under filtered colimits, equivalently if each representable h_U is compact (F ↦ F(U) commutes with filtered colimits). Representables are always coherent but need not be compact; their truncations are compact in Sh(𝒞)_{≤d} ([SAG, A.2.3]).
items.locator: Definition 3.4 and the preceding paragraph, p. 24

items.name: Excisive sites are compactly generated by finite sheaves
items.statement: Let Sh^f(𝒞) be the closure of the representables h_U under finite colimits. If 𝒞 is excisive, Sh(𝒞) = Ind(Sh^f(𝒞)). For a filtered system of excisive finitary sites 𝒞_i, the colimit 𝒞 is excisive and Sh^f(𝒞) = colim_i Sh^f(𝒞_i) via pullback. For d-truncated sheaves the analogous statements hold without any excisiveness hypothesis.

items.name: Local finite generation of π_d for finite sheaves
items.statement: Let 𝒞 be a finitary site, d ≥ 0, and F ∈ Sh(𝒞) with F_{≤d} in the finite-colimit closure of the (h_U)_{≤d} in Sh(𝒞)_{≤d}. Then there are finitely many U_i ∈ 𝒞 and x_i ∈ F(U_i) such that every section of π_0F is locally the class of some x_i; if d ≥ 1 and F is d-connective, these can be chosen so that each π_d(F; x_i) over U_i is generated by finitely many global sections.

items.name: Approximation by finite d-connective sheaves
items.statement: Let 𝒞 be a finitary site and d ≥ 0. (1) Any map F → G in Sh(𝒞) with F ∈ Sh^f(𝒞) and G d-connective factors as F → F′ → G with F′ ∈ Sh^f(𝒞)_{≥d} = Sh^f(𝒞) ∩ Sh(𝒞)_{≥d}. (2) If 𝒞 is excisive, Sh(𝒞)_{≥d} = Ind(Sh^f(𝒞)_{≥d}).
items.note: The printed proof has a misprint in its inductive step; see sourceIssues E1.

items.name: Finite d-connective sheaves under filtered colimits of sites
items.statement: Let 𝒞 = colim_i 𝒞_i be a filtered colimit of finitary sites and d ≥ 0. (1) If F ∈ Sh^f(𝒞_i) has d-connective pullback to 𝒞, it has d-connective pullback to some 𝒞_j. (2) If each 𝒞_i is excisive, Sh^f(𝒞)_{≥d} = colim_i Sh^f(𝒞_i)_{≥d}.

items.name: Homotopy dimension passes to filtered colimits of excisive sites
items.statement: If 𝒞 = colim_i 𝒞_i is a filtered colimit of finitary excisive sites and each Sh(𝒞_i) has homotopy dimension ≤ d, then Sh(𝒞) has homotopy dimension ≤ d.

items.name: Spectral spaces and spectral maps
items.statement: A spectral space is a topological space whose quasi-compact opens form a basis closed under finite intersections, and which is T_0 and sober (equivalently: T_0, quasi-compact, sober, quasi-separated, with a basis of quasi-compact opens). A continuous map of spectral spaces is spectral if preimages of quasi-compact opens are quasi-compact.
items.note: Mathlib/Topology/Spectral/Basic.lean and Hom.lean at 082e2d3: SpectralSpace extends T0Space, CompactSpace, QuasiSober, QuasiSeparatedSpace and PrespectralSpace (the quasi-compact opens form a basis); IsSpectralMap is continuity plus quasi-compact preimages of quasi-compact opens.

items.name: The prime spectrum of a commutative ring is a spectral space
items.statement: For every commutative ring R, Spec(R) with the Zariski topology is a spectral space.
items.note: Mathlib/RingTheory/Spectrum/Prime/Topology.lean:842 at 082e2d3 (the anonymous instance, named PrimeSpectrum.instSpectralSpace in the module docstring).

items.name: Hochster's theorem
items.statement: Every spectral space is homeomorphic to Spec(R) for a commutative ring R, and every spectral space is a filtered inverse limit, in spectral spaces and spectral maps, of finite T_0-spaces (finite spectral spaces) ([Hoc69, Prop. 10]). Consequently every partition of a spectral space into finitely many constructible subsets is refined by the strata of a spectral map to a finite spectral space.
items.locator: §3.2, footnote 5, p. 28; proof of Lemma 3.19, p. 32
items.note: D0 extends the spectral-space API with constructible and pro-constructible subsets, spectral maps, limits and profinite decompositions (ECD §2); the inverse-limit presentation by finite T_0-spaces is the statement used here.

items.name: Krull dimension of a spectral space
items.statement: The Krull dimension of a spectral space X is the supremum of the lengths n of chains x_0 → x_1 → … → x_n of non-identity morphisms in pt_X, i.e. of strict specialization chains; for sober X this is the supremum of lengths of chains of irreducible closed subsets, and for X = Spec R it is the Krull dimension of R.
items.note: Mathlib/Topology/KrullDimension.lean:40 defines topologicalKrullDim as the order-theoretic Krull dimension of the irreducible closed subsets; in a sober space these correspond to points ordered by specialization, which is the paper's definition.

items.name: Sheaves of spaces on a spectral space: points and connectivity
items.statement: Let X be a spectral space. The category pt_X of points of the topos of sheaves on X has the points of X as objects, with a unique map x → y iff every open containing y contains x ([HTT, Thm. 5.1.5.6, Prop. 6.1.5.2]). A sheaf of spaces F on X is d-connective (i.e. F_{<d} = ∗ internally) iff every stalk F_x is (d − 1)-connected, since sheaves of sets on X have enough points.

items.name: Finite approximation of spectral spaces of bounded Krull dimension
items.statement: Every spectral space of Krull dimension ≤ d is a filtered inverse limit, in spectral spaces and spectral maps, of finite spectral spaces of Krull dimension ≤ d ([Sal91, Thm. 3.2], essentially due to Isbell [Isb85], via Stone duality between spectral spaces and distributive lattices). Equivalently, for a qcqs algebraic space X the spectral stratifications |X| → S with dim S ≤ dim |X| are cofinal.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 3.12, p. 29; proof of Theorem 3.18, p. 35

items.name: Finite spectral spaces have homotopy dimension at most their dimension
items.statement: Let X be a finite spectral space (a finite T_0-space) and F ∈ Sh(X). If F is dim(X)-connective, then F(X) is nonempty.

items.name: The site of quasi-compact opens of a spectral space
items.statement: For a spectral space Y, the poset 𝒞_Y of quasi-compact opens with open covers is a finitary site with Sh(𝒞_Y) = Sh(Y) ([SAG, Prop. 1.1.4.4]); it is excisive, a presheaf being a sheaf iff F(∅) = ∗ and F(U ∪ V) ≃ F(U) ×_{F(U∩V)} F(V) (cf. [HTT, Prop. 6.5.4.4]); and if Y = lim_i Y_i in spectral spaces and spectral maps then 𝒞_Y = colim_i 𝒞_{Y_i}.

items.name: Homotopy dimension of spectral spaces with pointwise connectivity
items.statement: Let X be a spectral space of finite Krull dimension and F ∈ Sh(X) such that each stalk F_x is dim({x}‾)-connective. Then F(X) ≠ ∅; equivalently, if each F_x is (c + dim({x}‾))-connective then F(X) is c-connective.
items.note: The proof extends F to localizations of A (X = Spec A) by continuity and applies Zorn's lemma to localizations where F has no section, using a Zariski square along f and the localization at 1 + fA.

items.name: The étale site of a qcqs algebraic space
items.statement: For a qcqs algebraic space X, et_X is the category of étale maps U → X with U qcqs, and a sieve on U is an étale covering sieve iff it contains finitely many U_i → U with ⊔U_i → U surjective (nonempty pullback to every point); X_et is this site.
items.note: SF.1 constructs algebraic spaces and SF.2 owns the étale site and its cohomology; the paper's only extra requirement is that objects be qcqs, which makes the site finitary.

items.name: The Nisnevich site of a qcqs algebraic space
items.statement: X_Nis has underlying category et_X, and a sieve on U is covering iff it contains finitely many U_i → U such that ⊔U_i → U admits a section after pullback to every point of U. By [BH18, App. A] (for schemes; qcqs algebraic spaces have Nisnevich covers by affine schemes, [Ryd11], [SAG, Sec. 3.4.2]) this agrees with Lurie's definition, where an étale map is a cover if it has sections over the strata of a finite constructible stratification ([SAG, Sec. 3.7]).
items.locator: Definition 3.15(3) and the following paragraph, pp. 30–31 (introduced for noetherian schemes in [Nis89])

items.name: The Nisnevich site of a field
items.statement: For a field k, Spec(k)_Nis is the category of finite products of finite separable extensions of k (equivalently finite continuous Gal(k)-sets, 𝒯_{Spec k}) with the topology of finite disjoint unions: Nisnevich sheaves are exactly the presheaves preserving finite products, PSh_Π(𝒯_{Spec k}).

items.name: Spectral stratifications
items.statement: A spectral stratification of a qcqs algebraic space X is a spectral map p : |X| → S to a finite spectral space; its strata are the locally closed subspaces {s} ×_S X (with any structure sheaf; the statements do not depend on it). The spectral stratifications of X form a filtered system.

items.name: Constructible stratifications with finite étale pieces (Rydh)
items.statement: Let Y → X be an étale morphism of finite presentation of qcqs algebraic spaces. Then there is a finite stratification of X by constructible locally closed subspaces (hence a spectral stratification) over each stratum of which Y is finite étale.

items.name: Étale dévissage: qcqs algebraic spaces are Nisnevich-locally affine
items.statement: Every qcqs algebraic space X admits a Nisnevich cover by an affine scheme and a scallop decomposition: a finite filtration ∅ = U_0 ⊂ U_1 ⊂ … ⊂ U_n = X by quasi-compact opens with each U_{i+1} ∖ U_i (with its reduced structure) affine, glued along étale neighbourhoods ([Ryd11]; [SAG, Thm. 3.4.2.1, Def. 2.5.3.1]).
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 3.19, p. 32; proof of Proposition 4.34, p. 53; proof of Corollary 5.21, p. 63

items.name: Noetherian approximation and spreading out
items.statement: Every affine scheme is a filtered limit of affine schemes of finite type over Z with affine transition maps; étale morphisms of finite presentation, their sections and Nisnevich (split) coverings over the limit descend to some finite stage ([Stacks, Tags 01ZM, 07RP]).
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 3.19, p. 32; proof of Theorem 7.12, p. 82

items.name: Nisnevich covers split over the strata of a stratification
items.statement: Let X be a qcqs algebraic space and f : Y′ → Y a Nisnevich covering map of qcqs étale X-spaces. Then there is a spectral stratification p : |X| → S such that f admits a section over each stratum {s} ×_S Y.
items.note: The proof reduces to Y finite étale over affine, then noetherian X, and uses noetherian induction on the generic points.

items.name: The p-Nisnevich site
items.statement: For a spectral stratification p : |X| → S, X_{Nis,p} is the category of qcqs étale X-spaces in which a sieve on Y is covering iff it contains finitely many Y_i → Y such that ⊔Y_i → Y admits a section over {s} ×_S Y for every s ∈ S. It is a finitary site.

items.name: The Nisnevich site is the colimit of the p-Nisnevich sites
items.statement: As p runs over the filtered system of spectral stratifications of X, colim_p X_{Nis,p} = X_Nis as finitary sites, all transition functors and the identification being the identity of the category of qcqs étale X-schemes.

items.name: Excision characterization of p-Nisnevich sheaves
items.statement: Let p : |X| → S be a spectral stratification. A presheaf F on et_X is a sheaf on X_{Nis,p} iff (1) F sends finite coproducts to products and (2) for every closed Z ⊂ S and every map Y′ → Y in et_X that is an isomorphism over Z ×_S Y, F(Y) → F(Y′) ×_{F(U′)} F(U) is an equivalence, where U = (S − Z) ×_S Y and U′ = (S − Z) ×_S Y′. In particular X_{Nis,p} is excisive. In the limit over p this recovers the Morel–Voevodsky excision characterization of Nisnevich sheaves ([MV99, Prop. 1.4], [SAG, Thm. 3.7.5.1]).

items.name: Points of the p-Nisnevich topos
items.statement: For a spectral stratification p, Y ∈ et_X and s ∈ S, the functor F ↦ F_{Y,s} = colim F(U), over the cofiltered category of U → Y in et_Y that are isomorphisms over {s} ×_S Y, is the pullback functor of a point of Sh(X_{Nis,p}).

items.name: Sections of p-Nisnevich sheaves with highly connected stalks
items.statement: Let p : |X| → S be a spectral stratification and F ∈ Sh(X_{Nis,p}). If F_{Y,s} is dim(S)-connective for all Y ∈ et_X and s ∈ S, then F(X) ≠ ∅.

items.name: Homotopy dimension of p-Nisnevich topoi
items.statement: For a spectral stratification p : |X| → S: (1) the points F ↦ F_{Y,s} (Y ∈ et_X, s ∈ S) form a conservative family of points of Sh(X_{Nis,p}); (2) Sh(X_{Nis,p}) has homotopy dimension ≤ dim(S).

items.name: Pointwise criterion for sections of Nisnevich sheaves
items.statement: Let X be a qcqs algebraic space of Krull dimension d < ∞ and F ∈ Sh(X_Nis). If for every x ∈ X the Nisnevich pullback x^*F ∈ PSh_Π(𝒯_{Spec k(x)}) is d-connective, then F(X) ≠ ∅. The ordinary Nisnevich topos has enough points given by the finite separable extensions of the residue fields.
items.locator: Theorem 3.26 and the preceding paragraph, pp. 35–36

items.name: Nisnevich sheaves are hypercomplete
items.statement: Let X be a qcqs algebraic space of Krull dimension d < ∞. A map f : F → G of sheaves of spaces or spectra on X_Nis is an equivalence if x^*f is an equivalence for all x ∈ X; in particular all Nisnevich sheaves of spaces or spectra on X are hypercomplete (this is the Nisnevich half of Theorem 1.7).
items.note: Deduced from Theorem 3.26 with [HTT, Prop. 7.2.1.10, Rem. 6.5.4.7, Cor. 7.2.2.30].

items.name: Nisnevich cohomological dimension is at most the Krull dimension
items.statement: Let X be a qcqs algebraic space of Krull dimension d. Then X_Nis has cohomological dimension ≤ d.

items.name: Étale cohomological dimension bounds
items.statement: Let X be a qcqs algebraic space of Krull dimension d, 𝒫 a set of primes and cd_x the 𝒫-local cohomological dimension of the absolute Galois group of k(x). Then sup_x cd_x ≤ sup_{U→X ∈ et_X} CohDim_𝒫(U_et) ≤ d + sup_x cd_x; more precisely cd_x ≤ sup over Zariski neighbourhoods U of x of CohDim_𝒫(U_et). So for X of finite Krull dimension, the hypotheses of Theorem 4.36 hold iff the 𝒫-local Galois cohomological dimensions of the residue fields are uniformly bounded.
items.note: The first inequality uses continuity of étale cohomology ([Stacks, Tag 03Q4]) and exactness of closed pushforward; the second the Leray spectral sequence for X_et → X_Nis, whose stalks are the étale cohomology of the henselizations (noetherian case [Mit97, Thm. 2.8]).

items.name: Homotopy dimension of Nisnevich topoi with pointwise connectivity (schemes)
items.statement: Let X be a qcqs scheme of finite Krull dimension and F ∈ Sh(X_Nis) such that for each x ∈ X the Nisnevich pullback x^*F is dim({x}‾)-connective. Then F(X) ≠ ∅.

items.name: Cohomological and virtual cohomological dimension of profinite groups and fields
items.statement: For a profinite group G and a prime p, cd_p(G) is the least n with H^i(G, M) = 0 for all i > n and all p-primary torsion discrete G-modules M; cd_𝒫 uses 𝒫-primary modules. vcd_p(G) is cd_p of an open subgroup of finite cd_p (independent of the subgroup). For a field k, cd_p(k) and vcd_p(k) are those of Gal(k^sep/k); they differ only for p = 2, and vcd_2(k) = cd_2(k(√−1)) ([Ser94, §4]).
items.locator: Notation, p. 8; Theorem 4.26, p. 50; proof of Theorem 6.13 at 2, p. 75
items.note: Layer 11 defines cd_p, scd_p and cd for profinite groups (NSW III §3), including the behaviour under open subgroups needed for vcd; the field-theoretic identification vcd_2(k) = cd_2(k(√−1)) is Serre's.

items.name: The site 𝒯_G of finite continuous G-sets
items.statement: For a profinite group G, 𝒯_G is the category of finite continuous G-sets with jointly surjective families as covers; it is finitary and its sheaves of sets are the continuous (discrete) G-sets. PSh_Π(𝒯_G, 𝒟) denotes the presheaves carrying finite coproducts to products, equivalently presheaves on the orbit category 𝒪(G).

items.name: Sheaf criterion on 𝒯_G
items.statement: A presheaf F on 𝒯_G with values in an ∞-category 𝒟 with limits is a sheaf iff (1) F(X ⊔ Y) ≃ F(X) × F(Y) and (2) for every surjection T ↠ S of finite G-sets, F(S) ≃ Tot(F(T) ⇉ F(T ×_S T) ⇛ …).

items.name: Right Kan extension from objects over X
items.statement: Let 𝒞 have finite nonempty products, X ∈ 𝒞, 𝒟 have all limits, F : 𝒞 → 𝒟, and 𝒞′ ⊂ 𝒞 the full subcategory of objects admitting a map to X. The right Kan extension of F|_{𝒞′} to 𝒞 is Z ↦ Tot(F(Z × X) ⇉ F(Z × X × X) ⇛ …).
items.locator: Lemma 4.3, p. 39 (cofinality by Quillen's Theorem A, cf. [MNN17, Prop. 6.28])

items.name: Sheaves on 𝒯_G for a finite group G
items.statement: For G finite, a functor 𝒯_G^op → 𝒟 is a sheaf iff it is right Kan extended from {G}, so Sh(𝒯_G, 𝒟) ≃ Fun(BG, 𝒟); for a surjection G ↠ G′ with kernel N, restriction along 𝒯_{G′} ⊂ 𝒯_G corresponds to (−)^{hN}. Product-preserving presheaves are right Kan extended from the orbit category: PSh_Π(𝒯_G, 𝒟) ≃ Fun(𝒪(G)^op, 𝒟).

items.name: 𝒯_G as a filtered colimit
items.statement: For G profinite, 𝒯_G = colim_N 𝒯_{G/N} over open normal subgroups, hence Sh(𝒯_G, 𝒟) ≃ lim_N Fun(B(G/N), 𝒟) with transition functors (−)^{h(N/N′)}, and PSh_Π(𝒯_G, 𝒟) = Fun(𝒪(G)^op, 𝒟) ≃ lim_N Fun(𝒪(G/N)^op, 𝒟).

items.name: Postnikov sheafification on 𝒯_G
items.statement: For F ∈ PSh_Π(𝒯_G, Sp), extended by continuity to profinite G-sets, the Postnikov sheafification is F̃(S) ≃ Tot(F(G × S) ⇉ F(G × G × S) ⇛ …), functorially in finite G-sets S (motivated by the pro-étale site, [BS15]); analogously for presheaves of spaces.

items.name: Precomposition along morphisms of sites commutes with sheafification
items.statement: Let u : 𝒯′ → 𝒯 be a morphism of sites such that for each covering sieve h̃_t → h_t, π_0(u_*h̃_t) → π_0(u_*h_t) becomes surjective after sheafification on 𝒯′. Then u_* : PSh(𝒯) → PSh(𝒯′) commutes with sheafification (also for presheaves valued in a presentable ∞-category 𝒟), and u_* : Sh(𝒯) → Sh(𝒯′) commutes with colimits, n-truncations, Postnikov completion and hypercompletion. This applies when u has a right adjoint preserving covering families, e.g. Ind_H^G : 𝒯_H → 𝒯_G for H ≤ G open.
items.note: Routed here because Construction 4.7 (restriction to open subgroups) uses Example 7.3.

items.name: Restriction to open subgroups
items.statement: For H ≤ G open, u : 𝒯_H → 𝒯_G, S ↦ G ×_H S, is a morphism of finitary sites, and the induced u_* on sheaves commutes with all limits and colimits and with truncations, hence with Postnikov completion.

items.name: Weakly nilpotent group actions
items.statement: An action of a finite group K on a spectrum X is weakly m-nilpotent if the standard cosimplicial spectrum X ⇉ ∏_K X ⇛ … computing X^{hK}, coaugmented over X^{hK}, is weakly m-rapidly converging.

items.name: Uniform weak nilpotence implies Postnikov completeness on 𝒯_G
items.statement: Let F be a sheaf of spectra on 𝒯_G. If there is d ≥ 0 such that for every normal inclusion N ⊂ H of open subgroups the H/N-action on F(G/N) is weakly d-nilpotent, then F is Postnikov complete.

items.name: The sites 𝒯_G^N
items.statement: For N ≤ G open normal, 𝒯_G^N is the category of finite continuous G-sets with the finitary topology in which {T_i → T} covers iff ⊔T_i × G/N → T × G/N has a section; a product-preserving presheaf is a sheaf iff it has Čech descent for such surjections, and 𝒯_G = colim_N 𝒯_G^N.

items.name: Sheafification on 𝒯_G^N
items.statement: For F ∈ PSh_Π(𝒯_G^N, 𝒟) the sheafification is F_{G/N}(S) ≃ Tot(F(G/N × S) ⇉ F(G/N × G/N × S) ⇛ …) ≃ F(G/N × S)^{h(G/N)}.

items.name: Sheafification on 𝒯_G by the Čech formula
items.statement: Let 𝒟 be presentable and G profinite, and suppose (−)^{hK} : Fun(BK, 𝒟) → 𝒟 commutes with filtered colimits for every subgroup K of every finite quotient G/N. Then the sheafification of F ∈ PSh_Π(𝒯_G, 𝒟) is F^sh(G/H) = colim_{H′} F(G/H′)^{h(H/H′)}, over open subgroups H′ ≤ H normal in H.

items.name: Finite homotopy fixed points commuting with filtered colimits: truncated and coconnective targets
items.statement: (−)^{hK} for finite K commutes with filtered colimits when 𝒟 is a presentable n-category in which finite limits and filtered colimits commute (e.g. n-truncated spaces; totalizations are then finite limits, [HA, Lemma 1.3.3.10]), and when 𝒟 = Sp_{≤0} (test in Sp_{[−d,0]}).

items.name: Continuous cohomology of profinite groups through finite quotients
items.statement: For a profinite group G and a discrete G-module M, H^*_cont(G; M) = colim_N H^*(G/N; M^N) over open normal subgroups N.

items.name: Continuous cohomology as sheaf cohomology on 𝒯_G
items.statement: For an abelian sheaf 𝒜 on 𝒯_G with continuous G-module M, the Eilenberg–MacLane sheaf K(𝒜, 0) has K(𝒜, 0)(G/H) = colim_{N⊂H} (M^N)^{h(H/N)}, so π_*K(𝒜, 0)(G/G) = colim_N H^{−*}(G/N; M^N) = H^{−*}_cont(G; M), consistently with [SAG, Cor. 2.1.2.3]; for coconnective presheaves sheafification and hypersheafification agree.

items.name: Sheafification of module-valued presheaves
items.statement: For an E_1-ring R and a presheaf of R-modules on a site, sheafification may be computed in R-modules or in spectra: the unit map lies in the strongly saturated class generated by h̃_t ⊗ M → h_t ⊗ M, which become equivalences in both, and the forgetful functor preserves limits and colimits.

items.name: Hypercompleteness on 𝒯_G via weak nilpotence
items.statement: Let G be a profinite group of finite 𝒫-local cohomological dimension d and F a 𝒫-local sheaf of spectra on 𝒯_G. TFAE: (1) F is hypercomplete (equivalently Postnikov complete); (2) there is M with the H/N-action on F(G/N) weakly M-nilpotent for all normal inclusions N ⊂ H of open subgroups; (3) the same with M = d.

items.name: Hypercompletion on 𝒯_G is smashing
items.statement: If G is a profinite group of finite virtual 𝒫-local cohomological dimension, hypercompletion is smashing on 𝒫-local sheaves of spectra on 𝒯_G.
items.note: Abstract proof: Proposition 2.28 gives closure under colimits; tensoring with h_{G/H} is x_!x^*, and x_! preserves hypercompleteness after a splitting cover (Proposition 2.25).

items.name: Nilpotent objects with group action
items.statement: Let 𝒞 be stable, G finite and X ∈ Fun(BG, 𝒞). X is 0-nilpotent if it is a retract of an induced object ⊕_G Y; d-nilpotent if it is a retract of an extension of a 0-nilpotent object by a (d − 1)-nilpotent one; nilpotent if d-nilpotent for some d. For a family ℱ of subgroups, X is ℱ-nilpotent if it lies in the thick subcategory generated by objects induced from subgroups in ℱ. (d-nilpotent is 'nilpotent of exponent ≤ d + 1 for the trivial family' in [MNN17, MNN19].)

items.name: Basic properties of d-nilpotence
items.statement: In Fun(BG, Sp): (1) d-nilpotent objects remain d-nilpotent on restriction to any subgroup; (2) for d ≥ 0 they are closed under shifts, retracts and tensoring with any Z ∈ Fun(BG, Sp) (a tensor ideal); (3) a module over a d-nilpotent algebra is d-nilpotent; (4) if X is d-nilpotent and N ⊴ G then X^{hN} ∈ Fun(B(G/N), Sp) is d-nilpotent.

items.name: Nilpotence via skeleta of EG
items.statement: For G finite and X ∈ Fun(BG, Sp), X is d-nilpotent iff Σ^∞_+ sk_d(EG) ⊗ X → X admits a section in Fun(BG, Sp) (sk_d of the standard simplicial model of EG).

items.name: Nilpotence is detected on endomorphisms
items.statement: For 𝒞 stable, X ∈ Fun(BG, 𝒞) and d ≥ 0, TFAE: (1) X is d-nilpotent; (2) End_𝒞(X) ∈ Fun(B(G × G), Sp) is d-nilpotent; (3) End_𝒞(X) with the diagonal G-action is d-nilpotent.

items.name: Tate vanishing gives nilpotence for algebras
items.statement: Let G be finite and R an algebra in Fun(BG, Sp) with R^{tG} = 0. Then (1) R is nilpotent, and (2) if the underlying spectrum of R lies in Sp_{≥−d}, R is d-nilpotent. (Tate constructions vanish on nilpotent objects; the converse fails in general.)

items.name: Euler-class criterion for nilpotence relative to proper subgroups
items.statement: Let G be finite, ρ̃_G its reduced complex regular representation and e : S → S^{ρ̃_G} the Euler class. An object M ∈ Fun(BG, Sp) is nilpotent for the family of proper subgroups iff id_M ⊗ e^n : M → M ⊗ S^{nρ̃_G} is nullhomotopic for some n ≫ 0.

items.name: Thom isomorphism for complex representation spheres over HZ
items.statement: For a finite group G, HZ ⊗ S^{nρ̃_G} ≃ Σ^{2n(|G|−1)}HZ in Fun(BG, Mod_{HZ}).

items.name: Nilpotence criterion for HZ-algebras with G-action
items.statement: Let G be finite and R ∈ Alg(Fun(BG, Mod_{HZ})). If for each H ≤ G the underlying spectrum of R^{hH} lies in Sp_{≥−d} for some d ≥ 0, then R is d-nilpotent. The statement fails for algebras in Fun(BG, Sp) (trivial action on S, by the Segal conjecture, Remark 4.24).
items.note: The printed proof calls S^{ρ̃_G} 'the one-point compactification of G'; see sourceIssues E2.

items.name: Tate–Thomason nilpotence
items.statement: Let 𝔛 be an ∞-topos, 𝒜 a Postnikov complete algebra in Sh(𝔛, Sp), G finite and Y → X a G-Galois cover in 𝔛 such that Y/H has cohomological dimension ≤ d with π_n𝒜-coefficients for all H ⊂ G and n ≥ 0. Then every module over 𝒜(Y) ∈ Alg(Fun(BG, Sp)) is d-nilpotent; in particular Tate constructions vanish.
items.locator: Theorem 4.25, pp. 49–50 ([Ser94, Annex 1, Ch. 1], [Tho85, Rem. 2.28], [Mit97, Sec. 5.3])

items.name: Smashing hypercompletion and HZ-modules on 𝒯_G via nilpotence
items.statement: If G is a profinite group of finite virtual 𝒫-local cohomological dimension, then hypercompletion of 𝒫-local sheaves of spectra on 𝒯_G is smashing and agrees with Postnikov completion, and every sheaf of HZ_𝒫-modules on 𝒯_G is hypercomplete. The conditions of Theorem 4.26 imply that all Tate constructions F(G/N)^{t(H/N)} vanish; the converse is false (Example 4.15).

items.name: Extending Nisnevich sheaves to ind-étale algebras
items.statement: For X = Spec(A) and F a Nisnevich sheaf of spaces or spectra, left Kan extension extends F to ind-étale A-algebras commuting with filtered colimits; for B ind-étale over A the extension is a Nisnevich sheaf on Spec(B), since Nisnevich excision is finitary (unlike étale descent).

items.name: Henselization and strict henselization
items.statement: For an étale A-algebra B and 𝔭 ∈ Spec(B), the henselization B^h_𝔭 is an ind-étale A-algebra and a henselian local ring; the finite étale A^h_𝔭-algebras are equivalent to the étale k(𝔭)-algebras; strict henselizations are ind-étale and strictly henselian; the henselization is the colimit over étale neighbourhoods ([Stacks, Tags 04GE, 0BSK]); a finite algebra over a henselian local ring is a finite product of henselian local rings.
items.locator: Examples 4.31–4.32 and Construction 4.33, pp. 51–52; proof of Theorem 6.18, p. 78

items.name: Points of the Nisnevich and étale ∞-topoi
items.statement: For X = Spec(A), evaluation at an ind-étale henselian local A-algebra (e.g. B^h_𝔭) is a point of Sh(Spec(A)_Nis) (it commutes with colimits and finite limits, also for sheaves of spectra), and the ∞-category of points is the category of ind-étale henselian local A-algebras ([SAG, Sec. B.4.4]); evaluation at an ind-étale strictly henselian local A-algebra is a point of Sh(Spec(A)_et) ([HTT, Prop. 6.1.5.2], [SAG, Cor. B.3.5.4]).

items.name: Nisnevich pullback to a point
items.statement: For x = Spec k(𝔭) → X, the Nisnevich pullback x^* : Sh(X_Nis) → Sh(x_Nis) = PSh_Π(𝒯_x) is left exact and cocontinuous, given by (x^*F)(y → x) = colim F(U) over étale neighbourhoods y → U → X; for X = Spec A it is evaluation on finite étale A^h_𝔭-algebras.
items.locator: Construction 4.33 and the following paragraphs, p. 52

items.name: Reduction to affines
items.statement: Let X be a qcqs algebraic space and 𝒜 a Nisnevich sheaf of spectra on X. If for every p : U → X in et_X with U affine, p^*𝒜 is a sheaf (resp. hypercomplete sheaf, Postnikov complete sheaf, zero presheaf) on the affine étale site of U, then 𝒜 is a sheaf (resp. hypercomplete, Postnikov complete, zero) on X_et.

items.name: Étale descent is Nisnevich descent plus finite Galois descent
items.statement: On affine schemes, a presheaf of spectra is an étale sheaf iff it is a Nisnevich sheaf with finite étale (equivalently finite Galois) descent ([SAG, Thm. B.6.4.1]).

items.name: Hypercompleteness criterion on étale sites of finite Krull dimension
items.statement: Let X be a qcqs algebraic space of finite Krull dimension d whose residue fields have 𝒫-local cohomological dimension ≤ l, and F a 𝒫-local Nisnevich sheaf of spectra on X. TFAE: (1) F is a hypercomplete étale sheaf; (2) F is a Postnikov complete étale sheaf; (3) for every finite group G and G-Galois cover Y → Y′ of algebraic spaces étale over X, F(Y′) ≃ F(Y)^{hG} and the G-action on F(Y) is (d + l)-nilpotent; (4) for each x ∈ X, x^*F is a hypercomplete sheaf on 𝒯_x; (5) there is N ≥ 0 such that for every étale Spec A → X and finite G-Galois Spec B → Spec A, F(Spec A) ≃ F(Spec B)^{hG} and the G-action on F(Spec B) is weakly N-nilpotent.

items.name: Modules with finite étale transfers
items.statement: Let X be a qcqs algebraic space of finite Krull dimension with a global bound on the 𝒫-local Galois cohomological dimensions of its residue fields, and F a sheaf of 𝒫-local spectra on X_Nis such that (1) F has finite étale transfers: for every G-Galois cover V → U in et_X a genuine G-spectrum F_{V→U} whose presheaf on the orbit category agrees with F on the V/H (unique when F has finite Galois descent, by Borel completion, [MNN17, 6.3]); and (2) F is a module, compatibly with transfers, over a hypercomplete sheaf of algebras 𝒜 on X_et. Then F is a hypercomplete sheaf on X_et.
items.note: Requires genuine G-spectra, which nothing in the atlas plans; Corollary 4.40 has a second proof avoiding it. The printed proof has the wrong nilpotence exponent; see sourceIssues E3.

items.name: Chromatic localizations: L_1, L_{K(1)}, L_n^f, Morava K-theory and telescopes
items.statement: L_1 is Bousfield localization at complex K-theory KU and L_{K(1)} localization at the first Morava K-theory at an implicit prime p. For a prime p and n ≥ 0, K(n) is Morava K-theory (K(0) = HQ), T(n) a telescope of a type-n complex (T(0) = HQ), and L_n^f : Sp → Sp_(p) is p-localization followed by finite localization away from a type-(n + 1) p-local finite spectrum ([Mil92]); L_0^f is rationalization. L_1 and L_n^f are smashing (L_1T ≃ T ⊗ L_1S), T_Q ≃ (L_1T)_Q for every spectrum T, and L_1 kills every HF_p-module.
items.locator: Notation, p. 8; §5.4, p. 64; Example 4.15, p. 44; Examples 6.2–6.3, p. 69; proof of Theorem 6.13, p. 75
items.note: Nothing in the atlas plans Bousfield localization or chromatic homotopy theory; RefinedTraceMethods RT.4:topological supplies KU and ku.

items.name: Kuhn: Tate constructions vanish T(n)-locally
items.statement: For a prime p and n ≥ 0, Tate constructions of finite groups vanish in T(n)-local spectra, so T(n)-local homotopy fixed points of finite groups agree with homotopy orbits and commute with colimits; hence Proposition 4.12 computes sheafification of T(n)-local presheaves on 𝒯_G by the Čech formula.

items.name: A non-hypercomplete sheaf of spectra on 𝒯_{Z_p}
items.statement: For n ≥ 0 the constant sheaf K(n) on 𝒯_{Z_p} (computed in K(n)-modules by Proposition 4.12) has K(n)(∗) = colim_d K(n)^{BZ/p^d}. For n = 0 this is HQ. For n ≥ 1 it is even periodic with π_0 the ring of functions on T_p(𝒢) = lim_d 𝒢[p^d] for the height-n formal group 𝒢 over k defining K(n); for 𝒢 = Ĝ_m over F_p, π_0 K(1)(∗) = F_p[Q_p/Z_p]. The descent spectral sequence H^{−i}_cont(Z_p; π_jK(n)) ⇒ π_{i+j}K(n)^h(∗) gives k in every degree, so K(n) is neither hypercomplete nor Postnikov complete, although Z_p has cohomological dimension 1 and all Tate constructions of the finite quotients vanish. This answers [Jar10, p. 197] and also gives a non-hypercomplete sheaf of spaces via Ω^∞ (cf. Wieland's example, [HTT, Warning 7.2.2.31]).

items.name: May nilpotence conjecture (Mathew–Naumann–Noel)
items.statement: Let R be an H_∞-ring spectrum (for instance an E_∞-ring). An element of π_*R whose Hurewicz image in H_*(R; Z) is nilpotent is nilpotent. In the form used here and in [CMNN]: if R is an E_∞-ring with R_Q = 0, then L_n^f R = 0 for every n and every prime p.
items.locator: §1.2, p. 7; proof of Proposition 5.33, p. 67 (printed [MNN19]; the theorem is proved in Mathew–Naumann–Noel, J. Topol. 8 (2015))
items.note: See sourceIssues E5 on the citation.

items.name: E_2-spectral algebraic spaces
items.statement: An E_2-spectral algebraic space X = (X_et, 𝒪_X) is a site X_et with a Postnikov complete sheaf of (possibly nonconnective) E_2-algebras 𝒪_X such that (X_et, π_0𝒪_X) is the étale site and structure sheaf of a qcqs algebraic space π_0X and each π_n𝒪_X is a quasi-coherent π_0𝒪_X-module. Maps are maps of E_2-ringed sites that on π_0 come from maps of algebraic spaces; SpAlgSp denotes the ∞-category. Properties such as finite Krull dimension refer to π_0X.
items.note: The E_∞ theory is [SAG, Ch. 3]; the paper needs only E_2-structures throughout.

items.name: Étale E_2-algebras
items.statement: For an E_2-ring A and an étale π_0(A)-algebra A′_0 there is an E_2-A-algebra A′ with π_0(A′) ≅ A′_0 and π_*(A) ⊗_{π_0A} π_0(A′) ≅ π_*(A′), characterized by: maps A′ → B of E_2-algebras under A correspond to maps π_0(A′) → π_0(B) of commutative rings under π_0(A) ([HA, Sec. 7.5, Cor. 7.5.4.3]). Étale E_2-algebras under A form the étale site of π_0(A); a finite étale E_2-algebra B is canonically equivalent to B^op.
items.locator: Construction 5.2, p. 56; §5.4, Definition 5.22 and Remark 5.30, pp. 63, 66

items.name: Spec^et of an E_2-ring and étale maps of E_2-spectral algebraic spaces
items.statement: An E_2-ring A gives an E_2-spectral algebraic space Spec^et(A) on the étale site of Spec(π_0A); every E_2-spectral algebraic space is étale locally of this form. The étale site of X is X_et, a full subcategory of SpAlgSp_{/X}, and for Y → X étale and any Z → X, Hom_{/X}(Z, Y) ≃ Hom_{/π_0X}(π_0Z, π_0Y). An algebraic space over the sphere has the same étale and Nisnevich sites as its underlying ordinary algebraic space.
items.locator: Construction 5.2 and Definition 5.3 with equation (12), pp. 56–57; Remark 3.16, p. 31

items.name: Perfect modules on an E_2-spectral algebraic space
items.statement: Perf(X) is the full subcategory of 𝒪_X-modules locally in the thick subcategory generated by 𝒪_X; equivalently Perf is right Kan extended from affines, with Perf(Spec^et A) = Perf(A), by étale descent for perfect complexes over E_2-rings ([DAG XI, Thm. 5.4, Prop. 6.21]). Perf(X) is an associative algebra in Cat_perf (small idempotent-complete stable ∞-categories with Lurie's tensor product) and is rigid. The K-theory, THH and TC of X are those of Perf(X).
items.note: SchemeKTheoryOperations S.1 plans perfect complexes on schemes; the E_2 generality is new.

items.name: Quasi-coherent sheaves on an E_2-spectral algebraic space
items.statement: QCoh(X) is the presentably monoidal stable ∞-category of 𝒪_X-modules restricting on each affine Spec^et(A) to the sheaves A′ ↦ A′ ⊗_A M; since X is qcqs, QCoh(X) is compactly generated with compact objects Perf(X) ([SAG, Thm. 10.3.2.1], whose proof needs only E_2-structures).

items.name: Nonconnective K-theory, THH and TC of small stable ∞-categories
items.statement: Nonconnective algebraic K-theory K, connective K-theory K_{≥0}, topological Hochschild homology THH and topological cyclic homology TC as functors on small idempotent-complete stable ∞-categories (Perf of rings, E_1-rings and spectral algebraic spaces), with the cyclotomic trace K → TC.
items.note: K.6 builds nonconnective K-theory with localization for the enhanced categories S uses; RT.2 builds THH and TC of spectral categories; RT.3 the trace. The paper applies them to Perf(X) of E_2-spectral algebraic spaces (item 125).

items.name: Perf(X)-linear ∞-categories and exact sequences
items.statement: A Perf(X)-linear ∞-category is a left Perf(X)-module in Cat_perf, equivalently a left QCoh(X)-module among compactly generated presentable ∞-categories. 𝒞 → 𝒟 → ℰ is a fiber-cofiber (resp. split exact) sequence if Ind(𝒞) → Ind(𝒟) → Ind(ℰ) is a split exact sequence of QCoh(X)-linear presentable ∞-categories ([CMNN, Def. 3.8]); this holds iff it holds for the underlying stable ∞-categories (idempotent-completed Verdier quotients; linearity of the adjoints is automatic, [SAG, Rem. D.7.4.4], [HSS17, Props. 4.9(3), 5.4]).

items.name: Weakly localizing and weakly additive invariants over X
items.statement: A weakly localizing invariant over X is a functor from Perf(X)-linear small idempotent-complete stable ∞-categories to spectra sending fiber-cofiber sequences to fiber sequences; a weakly additive invariant sends split exact sequences to direct sums ('weakly': no commutation with filtered colimits is required, unlike [BGT13]). Such 𝒜 gives a presheaf Y ↦ 𝒜(Perf(Y)) on qcqs Y → X.
items.note: RefinedTraceMethods RT.5 plans localizing motives over the sphere; the weak, Perf(X)-linear variant over an E_2-base is not planned.

items.name: Examples of localizing and additive invariants
items.statement: K, THH and TC are weakly localizing invariants on all of Cat_perf and K_{≥0} is additive ([BGT13]); for a right Perf(X)-module ℳ in Cat_perf, 𝒞 ↦ K(𝒞 ⊗_{Perf(X)} ℳ) is weakly localizing over X, as − ⊗_{Perf(X)} ℳ preserves fiber-cofiber and split exact sequences (an (∞,2)-categorical condition; [CMNN, Sec. 3.2], [HSS17, Sec. 3]).

items.name: Base change from the connective cover
items.statement: Let X be an E_2-spectral algebraic space with connective cover X_{≥0} = (X_et, (𝒪_X)_{≥0}). For every U → X in X_et, Perf(X) ⊗_{Perf(X_{≥0})} Perf(U_{≥0}) → Perf(U) is an equivalence of Perf(U_{≥0})-linear ∞-categories.
items.locator: Lemma 5.13, p. 59 (quasi-coherent stacks, [SAG, Ch. 10, Thm. 10.2.0.2, Sec. 10.3.2]; precursors [TT90], [Toë12, Thm. 0.2])

items.name: Reduction to connective structure sheaves
items.statement: A weakly localizing invariant 𝒜 over X is also one over X_{≥0} via Perf(X_{≥0}) → Perf(X), inducing the same presheaf on et_X = et_{X_{≥0}}; hence descent statements for all localizing invariants reduce to connective X.

items.name: Nisnevich descent for weakly localizing invariants (Thomason–Trobaugh)
items.statement: Let X be an E_2-spectral algebraic space and 𝒜 a weakly localizing invariant over X. Then Y ↦ 𝒜(Perf(Y)) is a sheaf on X_Nis.
items.locator: Proposition 5.15, p. 60 (reduces by Corollary 5.14 to [CMNN, Prop. A.15], after [TT90]; the E_∞-structure there is not used)
items.note: SchemeKTheoryOperations S.4 plans Zariski and Nisnevich descent for K-theory of schemes (the case the Clausen–Mathew–Morrow extraction marked planned there); the statement for all weakly localizing invariants over E_2-spectral algebraic spaces belongs with Definition 5.1.

items.name: Étale base change for THH of E_1-algebras over an E_2-ring
items.statement: Let R → R′ be an étale map of E_2-rings, A an E_1-algebra in R-modules (THH(A) = A ⊗_{A⊗A^op} A is then an R-module) and B = A ⊗_R R′. Then R′ ⊗_R THH(A) → THH(B) is an equivalence of R′-modules.
items.note: The proof follows the dual of [HA, Prop. 7.5.3.6], using an idempotent lifting e ∈ π_0B ⊗_{π_0A} π_0B and a Tor spectral sequence.

items.name: Étale base change for THH with coefficients
items.statement: Let R be an E_2-ring, ℳ a right Perf(R)-module in Cat_perf and R → R′ étale. Then R′ ⊗_R THH(ℳ) → THH(R′ ⊗_R ℳ) is an equivalence of R′-modules.
items.note: Reduces to Theorem 5.17 by the R-linear Schwede–Shipley theorem ([HA, Thm. 7.1.2.1]), Morita invariance of THH (RT.2) and filtered colimits.

items.name: THH_ℳ is an étale Postnikov sheaf
items.statement: In the situation of Corollary 5.18, R′ ↦ THH(R′ ⊗_R ℳ) on E_2-rings étale over R is a Postnikov complete étale sheaf; indeed its presheaf-level Postnikov truncations are étale sheaves, since each π_k THH_ℳ is the quasi-coherent sheaf of the π_0R-module π_kTHH_ℳ(R).

items.name: TC is an étale hypersheaf (Geisser–Hesselholt, generalized)
items.statement: Let X ∈ SpAlgSp and ℳ a right Perf(X)-module in Cat_perf. The presheaf TC_ℳ(U) = TC(Perf(U) ⊗_{Perf(X)} ℳ) on et_X is an étale hypersheaf, and for every prime p, TC_ℳ/p is an étale Postnikov sheaf.
items.note: Proof: reduce to affines (Propositions 5.15, 4.34); TC is built from THH and TC(−;p)/p, TR^n from THH_{hC_{p^n}} by the fundamental cofiber sequence [HM97]; THH_ℳ/p is supported on the closed subtopos Spec(π_0R ⊗ F_p)_et, whose mod p cohomological dimension is ≤ 1 (item 155), so Proposition 2.28 applies.

items.name: Étale descent spectral sequence for TC_ℳ/n
items.statement: For n > 0 and an E_2-algebra R, the étale homotopy sheaves π̃_* of TC_ℳ/n have cohomological dimension ≤ 1, so TC_ℳ/n is a Postnikov sheaf and there are short exact sequences 0 → H^1(Spec(R)_et; π̃_{d+1}) → π_d(TC_ℳ(R)/n) → H^0(Spec(R)_et; π̃_d) → 0 for all d ∈ Z.

items.name: Galois nilpotence of TC
items.statement: Let X be a qcqs algebraic space, Y → X a G-Galois cover (G finite) and ℳ a Perf(X)-module in Cat_perf. Then TC_ℳ(Y) ∈ Fun(BG, Sp) is d-nilpotent for some d ≥ 0 (d = 4 when X is affine).
items.note: Rational spectra with G-action are 0-nilpotent; TC_ℳ(Y)/p^j is 1-nilpotent by Theorem 4.25 as a module over End(S/p^j) on the mod p locus.

items.name: Finite étale site and Galois extensions of E_2-rings
items.statement: The finite étale site of an E_2-ring A consists of étale E_2-A-algebras B with π_0(B) finite projective over π_0(A); it is equivalent to the finite étale site of π_0(A). B is G-Galois if π_0(B) is a G-Galois extension of π_0(A) (not the Galois extensions of [Rog08]).

items.name: Rational finite étale descent for additive invariants
items.statement: Let A be an E_2-algebra and 𝒜 a weakly additive invariant of A-linear ∞-categories with values in Q-module spectra. Then 𝒜 is a sheaf on the finite étale site of Spec(A); the key point is that a finite étale A → B defines a unit [B] ∈ K_0(A) ⊗ Q.

items.name: Finite étale descent for L_n^f-localized K-theory of rings (CMNN)
items.statement: For a commutative ring R (in particular π_0 of a connective E_2-ring), B ↦ L_n^f K_{≥0}(B) is a sheaf on the finite étale site of R; an additive invariant suffices, and for finite flat covers L_1K and L_1TC also satisfy descent.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 5.24, p. 64; proof of Theorem 6.9, p. 71 ([CMNN, Thm. 5.1, Prop. 5.4])

items.name: Dundas–Goodwillie–McCarthy theorem
items.statement: If A → B is a map of connective E_1-rings with π_0A → π_0B surjective with nilpotent kernel, the square formed by K and TC of A and B is a homotopy pullback: K(A) → K(B) and TC(A) → TC(B) have equivalent fibres.
items.locator: Proofs of Propositions 5.24 and 5.33, pp. 64, 67; Example 6.4, p. 69; proofs of Theorems 6.11 and 6.18, pp. 72, 77 ([DGM13])
items.note: RT.3 plans the relative nilpotent comparison theorem; the paper uses it to reduce from connective E_2-rings to π_0.

items.name: Finite étale descent for L_n^f K_{≥0} of connective E_2-rings
items.statement: Let A be a connective E_2-algebra. Then B ↦ L_n^f(K_{≥0}(B)) is a sheaf on the finite étale site of A.
items.note: By Dundas–Goodwillie–McCarthy reduce to π_0 (CMNN) and to L_n^f TC, which has finite étale descent by Theorem 5.16 and Corollary 5.21.

items.name: Additive noncommutative motives over an E_2-ring
items.statement: For an E_2-ring A, Mot_A is the presentable stable ∞-category of noncommutative motives with [−] : (A-linear ∞-categories) → Mot_A preserving filtered colimits and sending semiorthogonal decompositions 𝒞_1 → 𝒞 → 𝒞_2 to products [𝒞] ≃ [𝒞_1] × [𝒞_2], initial among presentable stable ∞-categories with such a functor. It is compactly generated by the [𝒞] with 𝒞 compact ([HSS17, Prop. 5.5]).
items.note: RefinedTraceMethods RT.5 plans localizing motives over the sphere; the additive, A-linear version over an E_2-ring is new here.

items.name: Corepresentability of connective K-theory in Mot_A
items.statement: Let 𝒞_1, 𝒞_2 be small A-linear ∞-categories with 𝒞_1 compact. Then Hom_{Mot_A}([𝒞_1], [𝒞_2]) ≃ K_{≥0}(Fun_A(𝒞_1, 𝒞_2)) naturally. ([BGT13] treats A = S and [HSS17] rigid symmetric monoidal bases; the arguments need only a monoidal structure.)

items.name: Functor categories between finite étale algebras
items.statement: Let A be an E_2-ring, B a finite étale E_2-A-algebra and ℳ A-linear. Then Fun_A(Perf_B, ℳ) ≃ Perf_{B^op} ⊗_{Perf(A)} ℳ (B is proper and smooth over A; [HA, Thms. 4.8.4.1, 4.8.4.6]). For A connective and B, B′ finite étale, Fun_A(Perf_B, Perf_{B′}) ≃ Perf(B ⊗_A B′), where B ⊗_A B′ is the finite étale E_2-algebra with π_0 = π_0B ⊗_{π_0A} π_0B′. (Additive K-theory of finite projective modules would suffice, Remark 5.28.)
items.locator: Proposition 5.29, Remark 5.30 and Corollary 5.31, pp. 65–66; Remark 5.28, p. 65

items.name: Finite étale descent for L_n^f-local motivic mapping spectra
items.statement: Let A be a connective E_2-ring and B finite étale. Then B′ ↦ L_n^f Hom_{Mot_A}([Perf(B)], [Perf(B′)]) = L_n^f K_{≥0}(Perf(B ⊗_A B′)) is a sheaf for the finite étale topology.

items.name: Nilpotence of Galois actions on L_n^f K_{≥0}
items.statement: If B is a G-Galois extension of a connective E_2-algebra A, the G-action on L_n^f K_{≥0}(B) is nilpotent.
items.note: By Dundas–Goodwillie–McCarthy and Corollary 5.21 reduce to discrete A, B; then (K_{≥0}(B)^{tG})_Q = 0 by the transfer argument of [CMNN, Thm. 5.1], so L_n^f(K_{≥0}(B)^{tG}) = 0 by the May nilpotence conjecture, and Lemma 4.22 applies.

items.name: L_n^f-localized noncommutative motives
items.statement: L_n^f Mot_A is the Bousfield localization of Mot_A at F ⊗ X → X for F a type-(n + 1) complex; since Mot_A is compactly generated, mapping spectra between compact objects are L_n^f-localized: Hom(L_n^f[𝒞], L_n^f[𝒟]) ≃ L_n^f K_{≥0}(Fun_A(𝒞, 𝒟)) for compact 𝒞, 𝒟.

items.name: Nilpotence of Galois actions on L_n^f-local motives
items.statement: If B is a G-Galois extension of the connective E_2-algebra A, the G-action on L_n^f[Perf(B)] ∈ Fun(BG, L_n^f Mot_A) is nilpotent.
items.note: Combine Proposition 5.33, Corollary 5.31 and Proposition 4.21, using that B ⊗_A B is (G × G)-Galois over A.

items.name: Detecting homotopy fixed points of nilpotent objects
items.statement: Let 𝒞 be stable, Y ∈ Fun(BG, 𝒞) nilpotent and X → Y^{hG}. Then X → Y^{hG} is an equivalence iff Hom_𝒞(Z, X) → Hom_𝒞(Z, Y)^{hG} is an equivalence for Z = X and Z = Y.

items.name: Finite Galois descent for L_n^f-local additive invariants
items.statement: Let A be an E_2-ring, 𝒜 a weakly additive invariant of A-linear ∞-categories with values in L_n^f-local spectra and A → B a G-Galois extension of E_2-rings. Then 𝒜(Perf(A)) ≃ 𝒜(Perf(B))^{hG}, and 𝒜(Perf(B)) is d-nilpotent as a G-object for some d depending only on A → B, n and p.
items.note: Equivariant algebraic K-theory ([Mer17], [Bar17], [BGS20]) could streamline the argument (Remark 5.38).

items.name: Étale descent for L_n^f-local localizing invariants
items.statement: Let X be an E_2-spectral algebraic space and 𝒜 a weakly localizing invariant of Perf(X)-linear ∞-categories with values in L_n^f-local spectra. Then Y ↦ 𝒜(Perf(Y)) is an étale sheaf on X.
items.locator: Theorem 5.39, p. 68 (extends [CMNN] from E_∞ to E_2)

items.name: Mod p étale cohomological dimension of F_p-algebras
items.statement: For every commutative F_p-algebra R and every p-torsion étale sheaf of abelian groups F on Spec(R), H^i(Spec(R)_et, F) = 0 for i > 1.
items.locator: Example 2.12, p. 12; proof of Theorem 5.16, p. 62; proof of Corollary 5.21, p. 63 ([SGA4, Exp. X, Thm. 5.1] and filtered colimits)
items.note: The same statement is Lemma 6.4 of Clausen–Mathew–Morrow, routed to this Part II by that extraction.

items.name: Rigidity of K^inv for henselian pairs (Clausen–Mathew–Morrow)
items.statement: For a henselian pair (R, I) and every prime p, K^inv(R)/p → K^inv(R/I)/p is an equivalence, K^inv = fib(K → TC). Combined with Dundas–Goodwillie–McCarthy it applies to connective E_1-rings R with π_0R commutative and henselian along I ⊂ π_0R.
items.locator: Example 6.4, p. 69; proofs of Theorem 6.11, p. 72, and Theorem 6.18, pp. 77–78 ([CMM21])
items.note: Clausen–Mathew–Morrow's Theorem A (Theorem 4.36 there), routed to this Part II by the extraction of PAPER-CLAUSEN-MATHEW-MORROW-21.

items.name: TC/p commutes with filtered colimits (Clausen–Mathew–Morrow Theorem G)
items.statement: For every prime p, R ↦ TC(R)/p commutes with filtered (indeed sifted) colimits of connective E_1-rings.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 6.6, p. 70; §1.1, p. 5 ([CMM21, Thm. G])

items.name: K-theory and TC agree p-adically at strictly henselian points of residue characteristic p (Clausen–Mathew–Morrow Theorem C)
items.statement: If A is a strictly henselian local ring with residue field of characteristic p, then K_{≥0}(A)_p̂ → TC(A)_p̂ is an equivalence (K^inv(A)/p = 0).
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 6.11, p. 72 ([CMM21, Thm. C])

items.name: Geisser–Levine: mod p K-theory of fields of characteristic p
items.statement: For a field k of characteristic p, π_i(K(k)/p) ≅ Ω^i_{k,log} for all i ≥ 0, K_i(k) has no p-torsion, and K(k)/p is log_p[k : k^p]-truncated.
items.note: The general Geisser–Levine theorem for ind-smooth local F_p-algebras is item 009 of the Clausen–Mathew–Morrow extraction, routed to this Part II.

items.name: Geisser–Hesselholt: mod p TC of fields of characteristic p
items.statement: For a field k of characteristic p, π_i(TC(k)/p) ≅ Ω^i_{k,log} ⊕ H^1_et(Spec(k), Ω^{i+1}_log) and the trace K(k)/p → TC(k)/p is the inclusion of the first summand; in particular TC(k)/p is log_p[k : k^p]-truncated and the trace is an isomorphism in the top degree.
items.note: Case of item 070 (Geisser–Hesselholt for ind-smooth F_p-algebras) of the Clausen–Mathew–Morrow extraction.

items.name: Gabber–Suslin invariance for strictly henselian Z[1/p]-algebras
items.statement: For every map A → B of strictly henselian local Z[1/p]-algebras, K_{≥0}(A)_p̂ → K_{≥0}(B)_p̂ is an equivalence; after L_{K(1)} the same holds for nonconnective K.
items.note: Combine Gabber rigidity (item 162, planned in KTheoryFiniteLocalFields L.2) with rigidity along extensions of separably closed fields, item 108 (Proposition 6.2) of the Clausen–Mathew–Morrow extraction, routed to this Part II.

items.name: Gabber rigidity away from the residue characteristic
items.statement: For a henselian pair (R, I) and n invertible in R, K(R)/n → K(R/I)/n is an equivalence.
items.note: L.2 plans rigidity with coefficients prime to the residue characteristic for the required henselian pairs.

items.name: Quillen: K-theory of finite fields
items.statement: K_0(F_q) = Z, K_{2j}(F_q) = 0 and K_{2j−1}(F_q) ≅ Z/(q^j − 1) for j ≥ 1; in particular K(F_p)_p̂ ≃ Z_p is concentrated in degree 0.

items.name: K-theory commutes with filtered colimits
items.statement: Algebraic K-theory commutes with filtered colimits of rings, and more generally of connective E_1-rings.
items.locator: Proofs of Theorem 6.6, p. 70, and Theorem 7.12, p. 82
items.note: K.7 plans filtered-colimit compatibility for rings; the extension to connective E_1-rings is part of the Part II's K-theory interface.

items.name: The motivic filtration on K-theory of fields
items.statement: For a field k of characteristic ≠ p the slice (motivic) filtration F^{≥n}K of [FS02], [Lev08] is a decreasing multiplicative Z_{≥0}-indexed filtration of Nisnevich sheaves on Spec(k) with lim_n F^{≥n}K = 0 and F^{=n}K ≃ Σ^{2n}HZ(n), the sheaf representing weight-n motivic cohomology; mod p, F^{=n}(K/p) ≃ Σ^{2n}HF_p(n).
items.note: M.6 constructs the filtered K-theory spectrum and identifies its layers with motivic complexes, using the corrected Levine/Friedlander–Suslin constructions.

items.name: Beilinson–Lichtenbaum (norm residue isomorphism)
items.statement: For a field k of characteristic ≠ p, every étale k-algebra A and n ≥ 0, HF_p(n)(A) ≃ τ_{≥−n}RΓ_et(Spec(A), μ_p^{⊗n}); for p = 2, HF_2(n)(A) ≃ τ_{≥−n}RΓ_et(Spec(A), F_2).
items.locator: Construction 6.14, equation (16), p. 74; proof at 2, p. 75 ([Voe03], [Voe11], [HW19])
items.note: M.5 plans the norm-residue theorem with its motivic-cohomology machinery, and M.7 deduces Quillen–Lichtenbaum from M.5 and M.6 through exactly this Beilinson–Lichtenbaum form.

items.name: Selmer K-theory
items.statement: For a small stable ∞-category 𝒞, K^Sel(𝒞) = L_1K(𝒞) ×_{L_1TC(𝒞)} TC(𝒞) (homotopy pullback along the L_1-localized cyclotomic trace). K^Sel(X) = K^Sel(Perf(X)) for an E_2-spectral algebraic space X and K^Sel(R) = K^Sel(Perf(R)) for an E_1-ring R. The natural map K → K^Sel factors both the trace K → TC and the localization K → L_1K.
items.locator: Definition 6.1 and the following paragraph, p. 69 (introduced in [Cla17])

items.name: Rational Selmer K-theory and Selmer K-theory away from p
items.statement: K^Sel_Q ≃ K_Q, since T_Q ≃ (L_1T)_Q for every spectrum T. If p is invertible on a stable ∞-category 𝒞, then p is invertible on THH(𝒞) and TC(𝒞), and K^Sel(𝒞)_p̂ ≃ L_{K(1)}K(𝒞) at the prime p.

items.name: p-complete Selmer K-theory of p-henselian rings is TC
items.statement: Let R be a connective E_1-ring with π_0(R) commutative and p-henselian (e.g. p-adically complete). Then L_{K(1)}K(R) → L_{K(1)}TC(R) is an equivalence (the square with L_{K(1)}K and L_{K(1)}TC of π_0(R)/p is cartesian by rigidity and Dundas–Goodwillie–McCarthy, and its bottom row vanishes since L_{K(1)}K(F_p) = 0 and both terms are K(F_p)_p̂-modules); hence K^Sel(R)_p̂ ≃ TC(R)_p̂.

items.name: Arithmetic square for Selmer K-theory
items.statement: For every E_1-ring R (and any localizing invariant) there is a pullback square with K^Sel(R), K^Sel(R_p̂), K^Sel(R[1/p]) and K^Sel(R_p̂[1/p]). For R connective with π_0R commutative of bounded p-torsion, after p-completion the terms are L_{K(1)}K or TC by Examples 6.3–6.4, and [BCM20] identifies the square with the p-completion of the defining square of K^Sel(R); p-adic L_1K and L_1TC depend only on π_0(R)[1/p] and π_0(R̂)[1/p].

items.name: Selmer K-theory is finitary and an étale sheaf
items.statement: (1) R ↦ K^Sel(R), from connective E_1-rings to spectra, commutes with filtered colimits. (2) On E_2-spectral algebraic spaces K^Sel is an étale sheaf; more generally K^Sel_𝒫 is, for every set of primes 𝒫, also with coefficients: K^Sel_𝒫(ℳ ⊗_{Perf(X)} Perf(−)) is an étale sheaf on X for any Perf(X)-module ℳ in Cat_perf.
items.note: (1) from TC/p commuting with filtered colimits (item 157); (2) from Theorem 5.39 for L_1K and L_1TC and Theorem 5.16.

items.name: fppf descent for Selmer K-theory
items.statement: On ordinary qcqs algebraic spaces, K^Sel is a sheaf for the fppf topology.
items.note: Finite flat descent for L_1K and L_1TC ([CMNN, Thm. 5.1]) and faithfully flat descent for TC ([BMS19, Sec. 3]) give finite flat descent; étale plus finite flat descent gives fppf descent ([Stacks, Tag 05WM]).

items.name: K(1)-local K-theory of F_p-algebras vanishes
items.statement: L_{K(1)}K(F_p) = 0, because K(F_p)_p̂ vanishes in positive degrees; hence L_{K(1)} kills every K(F_p)_p̂-module, e.g. L_{K(1)}K and L_{K(1)}TC of any F_p-algebra.

items.name: Suslin: K-theory of C with finite coefficients
