items.statement: K(C)/p → ku/p is an equivalence; more generally for algebraically closed fields of characteristic ≠ p, mod p K-theory is that of connective complex topological K-theory.

items.name: Automorphisms of p-complete KU
items.statement: The E_∞-automorphisms of KU_p̂ form Z_p^×, acting through Adams operations as scalar multiplication on π_2KU_p̂ = Z_p ([GH04]).

items.name: Drinfeld: K_{−1} of henselian local rings vanishes
items.statement: If R is a henselian local ring, K_{−1}(R) = 0.
items.locator: Proofs of Theorem 6.11, p. 72, and Theorem 6.18, p. 77 ([Dri06, Thm. 3.7])

items.name: Stalks of Selmer K-theory
items.statement: Let A be a connective E_1-ring with π_0(A) a strictly henselian local ring with residue field k. Then K(A) → K^Sel(A) is an isomorphism on π_n for n ≥ −1. For a prime p: (1) if char k = p, K^Sel(A)_p̂ ≃ TC(A)_p̂ ≃ K_{≥0}(A)_p̂; (2) if char k ≠ p, K^Sel(A)_p̂ ≃ (L_1K(A))_p̂ ≃ KU_p̂ as E_∞-rings, non-canonically, the choice pinned down by the canonical identification π_2(L_1K(A)_p̂) ≅ Z_p(1) from μ_{p^∞} ⊂ A^× = K_1(A).

items.name: Étale homotopy sheaves of Selmer K-theory with finite coefficients
items.statement: On a qcqs algebraic space X with connective structure sheaf, K^Sel → TC induces surjections π_d^et(K^Sel/p^n) → π_d^et(TC/p^n) whose kernel is 0 for d odd and j_!Z/p^n(q) for d = 2q, where j is the inclusion of the locus where p is invertible.

items.name: Lichtenbaum–Quillen for Selmer K-theory of fields, away from the characteristic
items.statement: Let k be a field and p ≠ char(k) a prime with cd_p(k) = d < ∞ (for p odd, or when √−1 ∈ k, cd_p = vcd_p). Then the fibre of K(k)_(p) → K^Sel(k)_(p) is concentrated in degrees ≤ d − 4 (so the map is an equivalence on (d − 2)-connective covers), and A ↦ K^Sel(A)_(p) is a hypercomplete étale sheaf on Spec(k)_et. Here K^Sel(k)/p ≃ L_{K(1)}K(k)/p.
items.locator: Theorem 6.13, p. 73, case p ≠ char(k) with finite cd_p ([RØ06]); proof in finite cohomological dimension, pp. 74–75
items.note: M.7 constructs étale K-theory by descent of finite-coefficient K-theory and deduces Quillen–Lichtenbaum with the degree range determined by the appropriate cohomological dimension. The paper reproves the case cd_p(k) = d < ∞ from Construction 6.14 and Lemma 6.15; the virtual case at p = 2 is item 182.

items.name: Lichtenbaum–Quillen for Selmer K-theory of fields of characteristic p
items.statement: Let k be a field of characteristic p with d = 1 + log_p[k : k^p] < ∞. Then K^Sel(k)/p = TC(k)/p, both K(k)/p and TC(k)/p are (d − 1)-truncated, the trace is injective and an isomorphism in degree d − 1, so the fibre of K(k)_(p) → K^Sel(k)_(p) is concentrated in degrees ≤ d − 4, and K^Sel_(p) is a hypercomplete étale sheaf on Spec(k)_et.
items.locator: Theorem 6.13, p. 73, case char(k) = p; proof pp. 73–74

items.name: Sheafifying a connective cover
items.statement: Let F be a sheaf of spectra on a site, G the presheaf τ_{≥j}F and G^sh its sheafification. Then fib(G → G^sh) is a presheaf of spectra concentrated in degrees ≤ j − 2.

items.name: Lichtenbaum–Quillen at 2 for fields of finite virtual cohomological dimension
items.statement: Let k be a field of characteristic ≠ 2 with vcd_2(k) = d < ∞ (so cd_2(k(√−1)) = d). Then K/2(k) → (K/2)^et(k), and hence K(k)/2 → K^Sel(k)/2, has fibre concentrated in degrees ≤ d − 3, and K^Sel_(2) is a hypercomplete étale sheaf on Spec(k)_et. The proof filters K/(2, u), u ∈ K_1 the class of −1 (image of t ∈ H^1(C_2; F_2) under RΓ(Spec A[i], F_2)^{hC_2}), whose graded pieces are étale hypersheaves in filtration ≥ d + 1, and removes u using nilpotence of η.
items.locator: Theorem 6.13 at 2 and its proof, pp. 75–76 (cf. [RØ05])

items.name: The class of −1 in K_1 is the image of the Hopf map
items.statement: For every ring A, the class u ∈ K_1(A) of −1 ∈ A^× is the image of η ∈ π_1S under the unit S → K(A); hence u is nilpotent.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 6.13 at 2, footnote 13, p. 76
items.note: Two proofs: via Barratt–Priddy–Quillen, η is detected by the sign of a permutation, the determinant of a permutation matrix; or by K_1(Z) ≅ π_1ko.

items.name: η-cofibre truncation criterion
items.statement: Let X be a spectrum. If the cofibre of η : ΣX → X lies in Sp_{≤n}, then X ∈ Sp_{≤n−2}. The proof uses nilpotence of η in the stable stems (η^4 = 0).

items.name: Multiplication by t on C_2-homotopy fixed points
items.statement: Let M be an F_2-module spectrum with C_2-action and homotopy in degrees [−d, 0]. For i ≥ d + 1 the map Σ^{−1}τ_{≥−(i−1)}(M^{hC_2}) → τ_{≥−i}(M^{hC_2}) given by t ∈ H^1(C_2; F_2) has cofibre M (as does t : Σ^{−1}M^{hC_2} → M^{hC_2}).

items.name: Lichtenbaum–Quillen and hyperdescent for Selmer K-theory
items.statement: Let X be a connective E_2-spectral algebraic space of finite Krull dimension and p a prime; for x ∈ X let d_x = vcd_p(k(x)) if char k(x) ≠ p and d_x = log_p[k(x) : k(x)^p] + 1 if char k(x) = p, and suppose d = sup_x d_x < ∞. Then (1) the fibre of K(X)_(p) → K^Sel(X)_(p) is concentrated in degrees ≤ max(d − 4, −2), so the map is an isomorphism in degrees ≥ max(d − 2, 0); and (2) K^Sel_(p) is a hypersheaf on X_et.
items.note: Reduce Nisnevich-locally to henselian local R (Corollary 3.27, Theorem 4.38), use rigidity ([CMM21], DGM) and K_{−1}(R) = 0 to pass to the residue field, and conclude with Theorem 6.13 and Lemma 6.19. The printed proof says 'R' for 'R′'; see sourceIssues E4.

items.name: Truncation of p-local spectra from rational and mod p information
items.statement: Let Y be a p-local spectrum with Y_Q concentrated in degrees ≤ d_1 and Y/p concentrated in degrees ≤ d_2. Then Y is concentrated in degrees ≤ max(d_1, d_2 − 1).

items.name: The big étale site of an E_2-spectral algebraic space
items.statement: The big étale site of X has all E_2-spectral algebraic spaces over X (of bounded cardinality) as objects, with the topology generated by finite families of étale maps Y_i → Y that cover in Y_et.

items.name: Big and small étale sheafification agree
items.statement: For F : SpAlgSp_X^op → Sp with big-site étale sheafification F̃, and every Y over X, F|_{Y_et} → F̃|_{Y_et} is the sheafification of F|_{Y_et} on Y_et. Consequently F is an étale sheaf (resp. hypersheaf, Postnikov sheaf) iff each F|_{Y_et} is.
items.note: An application of Proposition 7.1 (item 087), using that maps Y′ → Z étale-locally lift along étale covers Z′ → Z by (12).

items.name: Étale K-theory
items.statement: K^et is the étale sheafification of the presheaf of spectra K (nonconnective K-theory of Perf) on E_2-spectral algebraic spaces; by Proposition 7.6 it may be formed on the big or on the small étale site.
items.note: MotivicEtaleKTheory M.7 plans étale K-theory through descent of finite-coefficient K-theory spectra over fields and S-integers; this is the integral, non-noetherian sheafification.

items.name: The trace from étale K-theory to Selmer K-theory
items.statement: Since K^Sel is an étale sheaf (Theorem 6.6), the natural map K → K^Sel factors uniquely through K^et → K^Sel.

items.name: Axiomatic control of étale sheafification
items.statement: Let F : Alg_{E_2}(Sp)_{≥0} → Sp satisfy: (1) F commutes with filtered colimits; (2) F(R) ∈ Sp_{≤0} when π_0(R) is strictly henselian; (3) for compact R (π_0R is then a finitely generated commutative ring, [HA, Sec. 7.2.4]) F|_{Spec(R)_et} is d-truncated for some d. Then the étale sheafification F^et commutes with filtered colimits, takes values in Sp_{≤0} and is a hypercomplete étale sheaf.

items.name: Residue fields of schemes of finite type over Z
items.statement: If X is a scheme (or algebraic space) of finite type over Z of Krull dimension d, every residue field k(x) has vcd_p(k(x)) ≤ d + 1 for all p ([SGA4, Exp. X, Thm. 6.2]), and [k(x) : k(x)^p] ≤ p^d when char k(x) = p; so Theorem 6.18 applies to all such X.

items.name: K-theory is a Zariski and Nisnevich hypersheaf on qcqs spaces of finite Krull dimension
items.statement: Algebraic K-theory is a Nisnevich hypersheaf, in particular a Zariski hypersheaf, on every qcqs algebraic space of finite Krull dimension: it is a Nisnevich sheaf by Thomason–Trobaugh, and every Nisnevich sheaf there is hypercomplete. This supplies the non-noetherian case asserted in [RØ06, Thm. 4.1], whose reduction to the noetherian case would need uniformly bounded Krull dimension.

items.name: Nonconnective Selmer K-theory is an étale hypersheaf
items.statement: Let X be an E_2-spectral algebraic space of finite Krull dimension whose residue fields have bounded 𝒫-local cohomological dimension. Then K^Sel(−)_𝒫 is an étale hypersheaf on X, also with coefficients ℳ as in Remark 6.8.
items.note: From Theorem 7.14 (with n = 0 for the rationalizations) and Theorem 5.16, using the arithmetic square.

prerequisites.citation: Dustin Clausen, A K-theoretic approach to Artin maps, arXiv:1703.07842 (2017)
prerequisites.why: Introduces Selmer K-theory K^Sel = L_1K ×_{L_1TC} TC (Definition 6.1) and its role in Artin reciprocity.

prerequisites.citation: Dustin Clausen, Akhil Mathew, Niko Naumann and Justin Noel, Descent in algebraic K-theory and a conjecture of Ausoni–Rognes, J. Eur. Math. Soc. 22 (2020), 1149–1200
prerequisites.why: Étale and finite flat descent for telescopically localized K-theory and L_1TC (Theorem 5.1, Proposition 5.4), Nisnevich descent for localizing invariants (Proposition A.15) and the fiber-cofiber formalism (Definition 3.8), which §5 extends to E_2 bases.

prerequisites.citation: Akhil Mathew, Niko Naumann and Justin Noel, Nilpotence and descent in equivariant stable homotopy theory, Adv. Math. 305 (2017), 994–1084
prerequisites.why: Exponents of nilpotence (Definition 6.36), the cofinality statement of Proposition 6.28, the cobar criterion of Proposition 4.9 and Borel completion (§6.3), used throughout §4.1.

prerequisites.citation: Akhil Mathew, Niko Naumann and Justin Noel, Derived induction and restriction theory, Geom. Topol. 23 (2019), 541–636
prerequisites.why: Nilpotence for a family of subgroups and the Euler-class criterion used in the proof of Proposition 4.23.

prerequisites.citation: Akhil Mathew, Niko Naumann and Justin Noel, On a nilpotence conjecture of J. P. May, J. Topol. 8 (2015), 917–932
prerequisites.why: May's nilpotence conjecture, used in Proposition 5.33 and cited on p. 7 (printed as [MNN19]; see sourceIssues E5).

prerequisites.citation: R. W. Thomason, Algebraic K-theory and étale cohomology, Ann. Sci. École Norm. Sup. (4) 18 (1985), 437–552; erratum 22 (1989), 675–677
prerequisites.why: Bott-inverted étale descent, the rational transfer argument (Proposition 2.14 there, Proposition 5.23 here), the Tate–Thomason vanishing (Remark 2.28 there) and Proposition 1.39, which the paper's §§2 and 4 revisit. The erratum's DOI is 10.24033/asens.1596.

prerequisites.citation: Andreas Rosenschon and Paul Arne Østvær, The homotopy limit problem for two-primary algebraic K-theory, Topology 44 (2005), 1159–1179; Descent for K-theories, J. Pure Appl. Algebra 206 (2006), 141–152
prerequisites.why: Lichtenbaum–Quillen and hyperdescent for L_{K(1)}K away from the characteristic, including virtual cohomological dimension at 2 (Theorem 6.13, Theorem 6.18 for p invertible); Remark 3.31 repairs the non-noetherian step of their Theorem 4.1. The 2005 paper's DOI is 10.1016/j.top.2005.04.004.

prerequisites.citation: David Rydh, Étale dévissage, descent and pushouts of stacks, J. Algebra 331 (2011), 194–223

routes.title: Enhanced derived categories of sheaves, Part II: hypercompleteness of sheaves of spectra on Zariski, Nisnevich and étale sites
routes.brief:
First prerequisite: Enhanced derived categories of sheaves (EnhancedDerivedSheaves). E2 plans truncation and Postnikov towers, left completion, the finite-cohomological-dimension criterion and hypercovers for derived categories of sheaves, and this extraction makes Clausen–Mathew §2.1 a source for doing E2 for Grothendieck prestable ∞-categories and sheaves of spectra. This Part II adds the ∞-topos theory of hypercompleteness built on top of it: smashing hypercompletion, finitary and excisive sites, nilpotence criteria for hyperdescent, the homotopy dimension of Zariski and Nisnevich topoi without noetherian hypotheses, and the étale topos of a qcqs algebraic space as Nisnevich plus Galois.

Final theorems, as the paper states them (arXiv 1905.06611v3 numbering):
- Theorem 3.12 (Theorem 1.7, Zariski). A spectral space of Krull dimension d < ∞ has homotopy dimension ≤ d, so every sheaf of spaces or spectra on it is hypercomplete; Theorem 3.14 relaxes the connectivity pointwise.
- Theorem 3.18 (Theorem 1.7, Nisnevich). For a qcqs algebraic space X with dim |X| ≤ d, Sh(X_Nis) has homotopy dimension ≤ d; with Theorem 3.26, Corollaries 3.27–3.29 (stalkwise detection and hypercompleteness, Nisnevich cd ≤ d, étale cd bounds) and Theorem 3.30.
- Theorem 4.26 (Theorem 1.8). For G profinite of finite 𝒫-local cohomological dimension d, a sheaf F of 𝒫-local spectra on 𝒯_G is hypercomplete iff Postnikov complete iff every F(G/N) is d-nilpotent for H/N (N ⊂ H open, N normal in H) iff it is uniformly nilpotent.
- Theorem 4.36 (Theorem 1.6). Under a uniform bound on 𝒫-local étale cohomological dimension, F is a hypercomplete étale sheaf iff it is a hypercomplete Nisnevich sheaf and every x^*F is hypercomplete on 𝒯_x.
- Theorem 4.38. The five equivalent hypercompleteness conditions on the étale site of X of Krull dimension d with residue-field cohomological dimension ≤ l, including (d + l)-nilpotence of Galois actions.
- Corollary 4.40 (Theorem 1.9) and Corollary 1.10. Étale hypercompletion is smashing and equals Postnikov completion, and modules over étale hypersheaves of algebras (e.g. sheaves of HZ-modules) are hypersheaves.

Cover every construction on the way, in this order.
(1) Smashing hypercompletion (§2.2): Lemmas 2.22–2.23, Definition 2.24, the local–global principle (Proposition 2.25), strongly generating adjunctions and Proposition 2.28.
(2) Finitary sites (§2.3): Definitions 2.29–2.30, Propositions 2.31–2.32, nilpotent towers and rapidly converging cosimplicial objects (Definition 2.33), Lemma 2.34 and Proposition 2.35, importing the Dugger–Hollander–Isaksen construction (Proposition 2.36) from E2.
(3) Homotopy dimension (§3.1): Definition 3.1 and Theorem 3.2 ([HTT, Sec. 7.2.1]), filtered colimits of finitary sites, excisive sites and compact generation by finite sheaves, Lemma 3.8, Proposition 3.9 (correcting the misprint of sourceIssues E1), Proposition 3.10 and Corollary 3.11.
(4) Spectral spaces (§3.2): points and connectivity of sheaves on a spectral space, the Sancho de Salas–Isbell approximation by finite spectral spaces of Krull dimension ≤ d (prove it via Stone duality, or state it as an imported theorem with its exact hypotheses), Lemma 3.13, the excisive site of quasi-compact opens, Theorems 3.12 and 3.14.
(5) The Nisnevich site (§3.3): the Nisnevich topology on qcqs algebraic spaces with Bachmann–Hoyois's point-lifting description, the site of a field, spectral stratifications, Lemma 3.19, the p-Nisnevich sites with Lemmas 3.21–3.23, Proposition 3.24, Corollary 3.25, Theorem 3.26, Corollaries 3.27–3.29 and Theorem 3.30.
(6) Profinite groups (§4.1): the site 𝒯_G, its sheaf criterion and Lemma 4.3, Example 4.4 and Construction 4.5, Postnikov sheafification (Construction 4.6), restriction to open subgroups with Proposition 7.1 and Example 7.3, weak nilpotence and Proposition 4.9, the sites 𝒯_G^N and the Čech formula (Propositions 4.11–4.12, truncated and coconnective cases), continuous cohomology as sheaf cohomology (Example 4.13), Remark 4.14, Propositions 4.16–4.17, nilpotence in Fun(BG, 𝒞) (Definition 4.18, Lemmas 4.19–4.20, Proposition 4.21, Lemma 4.22), the Euler-class criterion of Mathew–Naumann–Noel and the Thom isomorphism HZ ⊗ S^{nρ̃_G} ≃ Σ^{2n(|G|−1)}HZ, Proposition 4.23 (with the fix of sourceIssues E2), the Tate–Thomason Theorem 4.25, Theorem 4.26 and Corollaries 4.28–4.29.
(7) The étale topos (§4.2): extension of Nisnevich sheaves to ind-étale algebras, points of the Nisnevich and étale ∞-topoi, the pullback x^*, Proposition 4.34, the Nisnevich-plus-Galois description of étale descent ([SAG, Thm. B.6.4.1]), Theorems 4.36 and 4.38, and Corollary 4.40 by its second proof (Theorem 4.38(3) and the tensor-ideal property). Corollary 4.39 needs genuine G-spectra and Borel completion, which nothing in the atlas plans; include it only with such a layer, correcting the exponent as in sourceIssues E3.

Import, never re-plan:
- EnhancedDerivedSheaves E2 (Postnikov towers, left completion, finite-cd criteria, hypercovers; this extraction adds Clausen–Mathew §2.1 and Proposition 2.36 as sources), E3 (Kan extensions) and E5 (monoidal stable ∞-categories, presentability, coherent group actions, the spectra comparison).
- StableHomotopyKTheory H.5–H.6 (spectra, Moore spectra, completion).
- SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.0–SF.2 (henselization and limit arguments, algebraic spaces with Rydh's stratification and étale dévissage, which this extraction routes to SF.0 and SF.1 as sources; the étale site and its cohomology).
- DiamondsAndVStacks D0 (spectral spaces and Hochster's presentation) and Mathlib's SpectralSpace, IsSpectralMap and topologicalKrullDim.
- Tau Ceti's ProfiniteCohomology layers 4, 10 and 11 (continuous cohomology through finite quotients, cohomological dimension).
The chromatic examples (Example 2.18, the T(n)-local case after Proposition 4.12, and the non-hypercomplete sheaf K(n) on 𝒯_{Z_p} of Example 4.15) go to the Selmer K-theory Part II proposed by this extraction, which owns chromatic homotopy theory and imports this Part II.

Unit tests:
- a rank-2 valuation ring and a non-noetherian ring of Krull dimension 1 (Theorem 3.12);
- the Nisnevich sites of a field and of a henselian discrete valuation ring (Example 3.17, Theorem 3.18);
- the constant sheaf HF_p on 𝒯_{Z_p}, which is hypercomplete, against Example 4.15;
- the trivial action of a nontrivial finite group on S, where Proposition 4.23 fails (Remark 4.24, Segal conjecture);
- Spec(R) for R the real numbers, with cd_2 = ∞ but vcd_2 = 0 (Corollary 4.40).

These extend E2 in its own direction, so they form a Part II of EnhancedDerivedSheaves rather than a new roadmap.

routes.title: Motivic and étale methods for arithmetic K-theory, Part II: Selmer K-theory and étale K-theory of spectral algebraic spaces
routes.brief:
First prerequisite: Motivic and étale methods for arithmetic K-theory (MotivicEtaleKTheory). M.5 plans the norm-residue theorem, M.6 the motivic filtration and M.7 étale K-theory by descent of finite-coefficient K-theory, with Quillen–Lichtenbaum for fields and S-integers. This Part II constructs integral étale K-theory by sheafification on qcqs E_2-spectral algebraic spaces and Selmer K-theory L_1K ×_{L_1TC} TC, and proves their hyperdescent and Lichtenbaum–Quillen theorems in all residue characteristics without noetherian hypotheses, together with étale descent and hyperdescent for L_n^f-local localizing invariants.

Final theorems, as the paper states them (arXiv 1905.06611v3 numbering):
- Theorem 7.12 (Theorems 1.1, 1.3, 1.5). For X a qcqs E_2-spectral algebraic space with connective structure sheaf: (1) K^et(X) → K^Sel(X) is an isomorphism on π_n for n ≥ −1; (2) if X has finite Krull dimension and the virtual 𝒫-local cohomological dimensions of its residue fields are bounded, K^et_𝒫 is a hypercomplete étale sheaf (with the descent spectral sequence, and every K^et_𝒫-module sheaf Postnikov complete); (3) K^et commutes with filtered colimits of connective E_2-rings.
- Theorem 7.13 (Theorem 1.2). With d = sup_x d_x < ∞ (d_x = vcd_p(k(x)) away from p, 1 + log_p[k(x) : k(x)^p] at p), K(X) → K^et(X) is an isomorphism on p-local homotopy in degrees ≥ max(d − 2, 0).
- Theorem 7.14 (Theorem 1.11) and Corollary 7.15. Étale hyperdescent for L_n^f-local weakly localizing invariants under finite Krull dimension and bounded mod p virtual cohomological dimension; nonconnective K^Sel_𝒫 is an étale hypersheaf.
- Theorem 6.18. The fibre of K(X)_(p) → K^Sel(X)_(p) lies in degrees ≤ max(d − 4, −2), and K^Sel_(p) is an étale hypersheaf.
- Theorems 6.6, 6.9, 6.11 and Corollary 6.12. K^Sel is finitary and an étale (indeed fppf) sheaf; K(A) → K^Sel(A) is an isomorphism in degrees ≥ −1 at strictly henselian A, with p-adic stalks TC(A)_p̂ or KU_p̂; the étale homotopy sheaves of K^Sel/p^n.
- Theorems 5.16 and 5.39. TC_ℳ is an étale hypersheaf with TC_ℳ/p Postnikov, and L_n^f-local weakly localizing invariants satisfy étale descent on E_2-spectral algebraic spaces (extending [CMNN] from E_∞).

Cover every construction on the way, in this order.
(1) Chromatic inputs: KU-, K(1)- and L_n^f-localization with smashing and T_Q ≃ (L_1T)_Q, Morava K-theories and telescopes, Kuhn's T(n)-local Tate vanishing, and the May nilpotence conjecture in the form 'E_∞ and R_Q = 0 imply L_n^f R = 0' (cite Mathew–Naumann–Noel 2015; see sourceIssues E5). Examples 2.18 and 4.15 (the non-hypercomplete K(n) on 𝒯_{Z_p}) live here.
(2) E_2-spectral algebraic spaces (§5.1–5.2): Definition 5.1, étale E_2-algebras and Spec^et, Perf and QCoh, Perf(X)-linear ∞-categories and their exact sequences, weakly localizing and additive invariants (Definitions 5.7–5.10), Example 5.12, Lemma 5.13, Corollary 5.14 and Proposition 5.15 (Thomason–Trobaugh, generalizing SchemeKTheoryOperations S.4).
(3) THH and TC (§5.3): Theorem 5.17, Corollaries 5.18–5.19, Example 2.12, Theorem 5.16, Corollaries 5.20–5.21. RefinedTraceMethods' henselian-pairs Part II needs Theorem 5.16 for Clausen–Mathew–Morrow's Theorems 6.3 and 6.5 (its item 111): export this layer to it, as EnhancedDerivedSheaves E4 and DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.1 export to each other.
(4) Finite étale descent (§5.4): Definition 5.22, Proposition 5.23, the CMNN descent theorem for rings, Proposition 5.24, additive noncommutative motives over an E_2-ring with the corepresentability of K_{≥0} (Construction 5.25, Theorem 5.26), Proposition 5.29, Corollaries 5.31–5.32, Proposition 5.33, Construction 5.34, Corollary 5.35, Propositions 5.36–5.37 and Theorem 5.39.
(5) Selmer K-theory (§6.1): Definition 6.1, Examples 6.2–6.4, the arithmetic square (Remark 6.5), Theorems 6.6, 6.9 and 6.11 with L_{K(1)}K(F_p) = 0, Suslin's K(C)/p ≃ ku/p, Aut(KU_p̂) = Z_p^× and Drinfeld's K_{−1}(henselian local) = 0, and Corollary 6.12.
(6) Lichtenbaum–Quillen (§6.2): Theorem 6.13 in characteristic p (Geisser–Levine and Geisser–Hesselholt), the virtual case at 2 (the class of −1 as the image of η, Lemmas 6.16–6.17), Lemma 6.15, Theorem 6.18 (with the fix of sourceIssues E4) and Lemma 6.19. The prime-to-characteristic case of Theorem 6.13 in finite cohomological dimension is M.7's Quillen–Lichtenbaum theorem: import it, or reprove it from M.5 and M.6 as §6.2 does.
(7) Étale K-theory (§7): the big étale site, Propositions 7.6–7.7, Definition 7.8, Construction 7.10, Proposition 7.11, the bound on residue fields of schemes of finite type over Z, Theorems 7.12–7.14 and Corollary 7.15, and Remark 3.31 (K-theory is a Nisnevich hypersheaf on qcqs spaces of finite Krull dimension).

Import, never re-plan:
- MotivicEtaleKTheory M.5 (norm residue and its Beilinson–Lichtenbaum form), M.6 (motivic filtration) and M.7 (Quillen–Lichtenbaum for fields).
- The Part II of EnhancedDerivedSheaves proposed by this extraction (EnhancedDerivedSheavesPartIIHypercompleteSheavesOfSpectra): hypercompleteness, homotopy dimension, nilpotence and the étale criteria (Theorems 3.18, 4.25, 4.26, 4.36, 4.38, Corollaries 3.27 and 4.40); and EnhancedDerivedSheaves E2 and E5.
- RefinedTraceMethods RT.2 (THH, TC, Morita invariance), RT.3 (trace, Dundas–Goodwillie–McCarthy), RT.4:topological (KU, ku), RT.5 (localizing motives), and its henselian-pairs Part II (RefinedTraceMethodsPartIIHenselianPairs): rigidity for henselian pairs, TC/p finitary, Theorem C, Geisser–Levine, Geisser–Hesselholt, the mod p cohomological dimension of F_p-algebras and Gabber–Suslin invariance.
- GeneralAlgebraicKTheory K.6 (nonconnective K, localization) and K.7 (filtered colimits); SchemeKTheoryOperations S.1 and S.4; KTheoryFiniteLocalFields L.1 (Quillen) and L.2 (Gabber rigidity); StableHomotopyKTheory H.5–H.6.
- SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.0–SF.2 and Tau Ceti's ProfiniteCohomology layer 11 (cd and vcd).

Unit tests:
- a separably closed field of characteristic ≠ p (Theorem 6.11(2), KU_p̂) and F̄_p (Theorem 6.11(1));
- Spec Z_p and Spec Z[1/p], where d = 2 in Theorem 7.13;
- the real numbers, with vcd_2 = 0 but cd_2 = ∞ (Theorem 6.13 at 2);
- F_p(t), with d = 2 in characteristic p;
- the C_2-Galois extension R ⊂ C, where L_1K(R) ≃ L_1K(C)^{hC_2} (Proposition 5.37);
- Example 4.15 for n = 1, with π_0 = F_p[Q_p/Z_p].

The paper's integral étale K-theory on non-noetherian E_2-spectral algebraic spaces, Selmer K-theory, the p-adic comparison through TC and hyperdescent for L_n^f-local invariants go further in exactly that direction. Nothing in the atlas plans E_2-spectral algebraic spaces, Bousfield or chromatic localization, or étale descent for localizing invariants, so these are new layers of a MotivicEtaleKTheory Part II.

routes.title: Hochschild, cyclotomic and refined trace methods, Part II: K-theory and topological cyclic homology of henselian pairs
routes.reason: The Clausen–Mathew–Morrow extraction proposes this Part II and routes to it rigidity for henselian pairs, Theorems C and G, Geisser–Levine, Geisser–Hesselholt, the mod p cohomological dimension of F_p-algebras and Suslin's rigidity for separably closed fields; routing the same inputs here keeps one owner for them.

E2 plans truncation and Postnikov towers, the left completion, the finite-cohomological-dimension criterion, hypercovers and totalizations for derived categories of sheaves, and already receives the hyperdescent results of Bhatt–Scholze. Clausen–Mathew §2.1 and Proposition 2.36 state the same standard facts for Grothendieck prestable ∞-categories, which include 𝒟(𝒜)_{≥0} and sheaves of spectra: a source for E2 at that generality.

SF.1 constructs algebraic spaces; Rydh's stratification of an étale morphism into finite étale pieces and his étale dévissage (qcqs algebraic spaces are Nisnevich-locally affine, with scallop decompositions) are structure results about them.

Henselization, strict henselization and noetherian approximation are standard Stacks-project commutative algebra and limit arguments; the Clausen–Mathew–Morrow extraction routes henselization of pairs to SF.0, and these belong with it.
